ALMOST ONE-SHOT FEEL.
The whole scene should play as one flowing, continuous cinematic shot with no fast cuts and no montage. If a cut exists at all, it must feel invisible and fully hidden inside movement, so the sequence plays like a near one-take.
Start EXTREMELY CLOSE on Adam asleep in bed inside the caravan.
He is wearing a white ribbed undershirt and black suit trousers, as if he passed out still dressed after a long night.
He is not waking in panic.
He simply opens his eyes and needs a short moment to orient himself.
The feeling is subtle:
he wakes, blinks, and for a brief second thinks,
“Where did I wake up again?”
No shock.
No big fright.
No melodramatic reaction.
His eyes open.
A short blank beat.
A small, quiet reorientation.
He looks around the caravan interior briefly, still hazy and not fully present yet.
Keep this understated and believable.
His face shows exhaustion and light disorientation, but only in a muted, realistic way.
Most importantly, his body should move SLOWLY.
He is still groggy.
He is slightly spaced-out, slightly hungover, slightly foggy.
His brain has not caught up yet.
Do not let him move efficiently or quickly.
Every movement should feel delayed, heavy and a little verballert, like he is only gradually returning to himself.
The camera stays very close and intimate at first, with tiny handheld micro-drift, as if we are trapped in the cramped caravan with him.
As he slowly props himself up, the camera gently pulls back just enough to reveal more of the bed and the narrow caravan around him.
He sits upright and quietly gathers himself.
Then he looks down and notices a plain WHITE DRESS SHIRT lying on the FLOOR beside the bed.
This is important:
the shirt is not hanging anywhere and not lying neatly nearby.
It is on the floor.
Adam slowly bends down and simply grabs the shirt from the floor in a tired, absent-minded way.
He pulls the white shirt on over the white ribbed undershirt.
He keeps the black suit trousers on.
The shirt sits slightly loose and unpolished, like he is only half getting himself together.
Adam has NO HAND TATTOOS.
This is important:
his hands must be completely free of tattoos.
Arm tattoos are okay, but the hands themselves must remain clean and untattooed.
The camera observes closely and stays physically near him in the cramped space.
From here, the camera begins to move WITH him through the caravan in a slow, natural, observational flow.
The key idea is that we stay with him and accompany him all the way to the door.
He stands and moves toward the small mirror.
The mirror moment should stay strong and cinematic.
Do not overplay it emotionally.
It should feel casual and human:
he catches himself briefly in the mirror while still waking up.
Let the camera drift so we can see him in reflection for a short beat.
Around the mirror, keep small caravan details visible in soft focus:
toothbrush, minor toiletries, worn surfaces, tiny everyday clutter.
Adam looks at his own reflection like he is checking reality for a second.
He looks tired, slightly distant, and still not fully there yet.
Then he turns away and continues toward the caravan door.
From here the camera stays with him and moves in front of him, gently backing up through the narrow interior as he walks.
The motion must feel human and cinematic:
not gimbal-perfect,
not shaky,
not stylized,
just controlled handheld intimacy.
Keep Adam’s walking pace slow and a little foggy.
He has just woken up.
He should not feel crisp or fully switched on yet.
When he reaches the caravan door, he opens it.
Cold pale morning light spills in.
The exposure lifts naturally as the door opens.
The camera continues backward and goes out with him, transitioning from the cramped interior to just outside the caravan door in one smooth move.
Adam follows and steps outside.
Stay with him just beyond the threshold so it feels like we truly went out with him.
Once outside, Adam looks ahead and reacts very subtly, as if he has noticed something that surprises him just a little.
Not fear.
Not horror.
Just a quiet, slightly puzzled look, like he has seen something unexpected and is trying to understand it.
This outside reaction should be small, restrained and intriguing.
The scene ends just after stepping outside the caravan, with Adam in the cool morning air, now awake, slightly grounded, and faintly wondering about what he sees.
CAMERA RHYTHM:
extreme intimate opening →
gentle wake-up with brief orientation →
subtle pullback as he gathers himself →
slow grab of the shirt from the floor →
close observational follow through the caravan →
strong mirror beat →
camera moves backward with him toward the door →
seamless move outside with him →
quiet, subtle final look of mild surprise.
SOUND:
No music.
Only natural sound.
Morning breathing,
fabric movement,
mattress creak,
shirt fabric,
soft footsteps,
small caravan interior sounds,
door handle,
door opening,
distant wind,
subtle campsite ambience appearing more clearly once the door opens.
NEGATIVE:
no fast cuts,
no flashy camera moves,
no dreamlike surrealism,
no glossy beauty light,
no oversaturated grade,
no fashion energy,
no melodramatic panic,
no broad acting,
no hand tattoos,
no perfect gimbal movement.

faces
bodies
hands
clothing
silhouettes

subtle
wispy
irregular
translucent
softly illuminated by the warm light coming from below

SHOT
An extremely low, foot-level cinematic action shot inside a dense cornfield at night.
The camera is only 10–15 cm above the ground, almost scraping through the soil, positioned directly inside the narrow passage between the corn rows.
We see absolutely no faces or upper bodies. Only legs, feet, corn stalks and the ground.
In the immediate foreground, Sicko is moving quickly through the cornfield, closest to the lens.
His worn dark reddish-brown low cowboy ankle boots dominate the foreground, partially covered by his wide black corduroy trousers, exactly as in the reference look. The trousers must fall naturally onto the boots and visually belong to them — no cropped trouser length, no awkward gap above the shoe, no slim fit, no styling mismatch.
Several feet behind him follows Adam, clearly visible as the second layer of the composition.
Adam wears his wide brown corduroy trousers and black leather loafers with the small gold buckle, matching the established reference styling. His trousers must also sit naturally on the shoes with the correct weight and break — cohesive, believable, and consistent with the reference images.
The spacing must read clearly:
Sicko foreground → Adam background → deep corn corridor behind them.
The corn rows are extremely narrow and overgrown. Thick stalks and large leaves constantly invade the frame from both sides.
Some leaves pass extremely close to the lens, partially obscuring the foreground and creating aggressive natural foreground depth. Other leaves are bent backwards by the men’s legs as they force their way through.
The ground is dark, damp and uneven:
crushed leaves
exposed soil
broken corn husks
small patches of mud
vegetation being kicked aside
The image must feel like we are physically running through the field with them, not observing them safely from outside.
ACTION / ENERGY
The frame must contain strong implied movement.
Sicko’s front boot lands heavily into the soil while the other leg is already driving forward.
Adam is caught one step behind him.
Corn leaves whip sideways from their movement.
A few leaves very close to camera carry subtle natural motion blur, while the foreground boot remains sharply readable.
Loose dirt and tiny plant fragments are disturbed underneath their shoes.
The trousers move naturally around their ankles.
Nothing feels posed.
Nothing looks like two models simply standing in a cornfield.
This should feel like a single stolen frame from a tense, kinetic chase through the crops.
CAMERA
35mm Zeiss Super Speed Mk II, T2.0.
Extremely low horizontal perspective.
Camera almost touches the ground.
Close physical proximity to Sicko’s boots.
Strong exaggerated foreground-to-background depth.
Sicko’s nearest boot is critically sharp.
Adam’s shoes remain recognizable slightly deeper inside the frame.
Corn stalks create multiple visual layers:
blurred leaves inches from lens → Sicko → Adam → repeating rows disappearing into darkness.
Slight human handheld imperfection, as though a camera operator is moving through the corn directly behind them.
No polished gimbal feeling.
LIGHT
It must feel like real natural night.
No frontal lighting. No fill from camera direction. No visible source lighting the subjects from the front. No movie key light.
The scene is illuminated only by very weak natural ambient night light — faint sky spill and minimal environmental night exposure filtering through the corn.
The light should fall unevenly and naturally across the leaves, trousers, shoes and wet ground.
Faces are not visible, and nothing should appear intentionally lit.
The darkness between the rows should stay deep and believable.
The image must be readable, but it should never feel illuminated for the camera.
No rim-light styling, no blue Hollywood moonlight, no artificial spotlight, no clean cinematic front exposure.
COMPOSITION PRIORITY

The corn must not merely be background scenery.
It surrounds the camera.
Leaves cross the foreground.
Stalks create vertical lines around the legs.

SHOT:
A breathtaking but completely realistic sunrise over the Baltic Sea, seen from the elevated coastal tower.

The horizon is the absolute focus.

The sun sits extremely low, only just breaking through a narrow opening between a dense cool-gray cloud ceiling and the sea horizon.

Instead of a small pale sun, create a wide luminous band of warm light stretching across the entire horizon.

cold blue-gray upper clouds,
soft mauve-gray transitions,
dusty rose,
muted coral,
pale peach,
warm apricot,
and a thin almost white-golden strip directly around the rising sun.

The transition between these colors is extremely soft and atmospheric.

SEA:

A long soft reflection of the sun travels across the water toward the camera.

Large open negative space.

Simple, powerful composition.

The warm sunlight should gently bloom through the Black Pro-Mist without losing detail.

melancholy.

dense clouds,

slightly matte
faintly textured
simple outdoor camping-table character
no decoration
no tablecloth
no wood
no metal table

A single small mosquito circles slowly and irregularly around the flame of the tealight.

No swarm.
Only one mosquito.

the white plastic tabletop around the candle remains visible and fairly legible

tiny antennae
natural proportions

mosquito
night darkness around it

Preserve the fundamental spatial structure of the location, but extend the rave deeper underneath the bridge so the camera can physically move from outside the party into the dancefloor.
EXACT LOCATION
A secret illegal nighttime rave underneath a massive elevated concrete highway bridge in rural eastern Germany.
The bridge is enormous and brutally utilitarian:
two broad parallel concrete highway decks overhead
huge rectangular concrete support columns
repetitive columns disappearing far into the distance
raw weathered concrete
no decoration
no festival infrastructure
no commercial branding
no stage construction
The bridge itself creates a long, dark architectural tunnel.
The rave occupies this tunnel.
FOREGROUND — OUTSIDE THE RAVE
The camera begins just outside the party area.
Directly ahead is a narrow wet dirt and concrete access path leading underneath the bridge.
The ground is:
uneven
muddy
partially covered in shallow puddles
visibly damp from recent rain
Red lights from the rave reflect organically in the puddles.
On the right side, a dense mature cornfield grows almost directly against the access path.
Tall corn plants form a dark wall approximately human height or higher.
The plants partially conceal the rave when approaching from this direction.
On the left side, the terrain drops slightly toward wild grass, weeds and rough industrial vegetation.
A rusty old metal railing runs through part of the foreground.
Beyond it, in the darkness, stands a distant industrial facility with:
pipes
tanks
chimneys
metal structures
a few dirty white industrial lights
occasional tiny red warning lights
The industrial plant remains distant and secondary.
THE ENTRANCE INTO THE RAVE
There is NO formal entrance.
No gate.
No security.
No ticket booth.
No sign.
No festival arch.
The access path simply continues underneath the bridge and gradually turns into the dancefloor.
This transition should feel almost accidental:
empty wet path → scattered people → small groups → dense dancing crowd.
There must always remain a believable narrow passage through the center of the people so the camera can continue moving forward.
People occasionally cross the camera's path.
Someone steps aside.
Someone walks toward the rave carrying a drink.
Two people stand talking near a bridge column.
But there is never a perfectly clear artificial corridor.
The camera has to naturally weave its way into the crowd.
DANCEFLOOR GEOGRAPHY — ABSOLUTELY CRITICAL
The dancefloor begins approximately underneath the first major bridge columns and continues much deeper underneath the bridge.
Do NOT create one compact crowd standing far away.
Instead create a long, organically distributed underground-rave crowd extending through several bridge spans.
Closest to camera:
around 5–10 scattered people.
Further inside:
20–40 people dancing and standing in loose groups.
Deeper underneath the bridge:
the crowd becomes denser and disappears into darkness, red light and atmospheric haze.
The party should visually continue far beyond what the camera can immediately see.
The repeating concrete columns divide the rave naturally into several loose zones.
The people occupy the spaces between the columns, never blocking the architecture completely.
The bridge must still feel enormous compared with the humans.
LIGHTING
Lighting is extremely minimal and improvised.
Small vertical red practical lights are positioned irregularly beside several concrete columns.
They are simple underground-rave lighting sources, not professional concert fixtures.
The nearest columns receive strong patches of dirty saturated red light.
Other areas fall almost completely into darkness.
The red light catches:
concrete surfaces
wet ground
smoke
silhouettes
faces for brief moments
No rainbow lighting.
No polished club lighting.
No giant LED screens.
No lasers dominating the frame.
No festival stage.
The dominant color relationship is:
deep blue-black night + cold industrial darkness + dirty red practical light.
ATMOSPHERE
A moderate amount of smoke or haze hangs underneath the bridge.
It collects deeper inside the rave and catches the red lights.
It must feel like real party haze mixed with damp night air — not cinematic fog covering the entire location.
The air is humid.
The concrete is wet.
The vegetation is wet.
The ground reflects light.
Everything feels slightly dirty and temporary.
CROWD
This is an underground European rave, not a commercial EDM festival.
The crowd is relatively young and alternative.
Clothing is mostly:
black
dark gray
washed dark fabrics
oversized jackets
hoodies
technical clothing
worn leather
occasional provocative underground club clothing
Some people dance intensely.
Others barely move.
Some smoke.
Some talk beside the columns.
Some wander through the crowd.
Nobody performs for the camera.
No synchronized dancing.
No cheering festival crowd.
No phones raised into the air.
The rave should feel discovered rather than staged.
CAMERA ENTRY
The visual composition must create a very strong forward axis underneath the bridge.
The bridge decks, repeating columns and wet access path all lead the eye directly toward the rave.
The camera has a believable physical route:
cornfield edge → wet access path → first people → illuminated bridge columns → dancefloor → dense interior of the rave.
The deeper the camera moves underneath the bridge, the more the outside world disappears.
The cornfield and industrial plant gradually become invisible behind the camera.
The concrete bridge structure surrounds the viewer.
People increasingly fill the frame.
Red light becomes stronger.
Music becomes louder.
The camera eventually feels completely absorbed into the rave.
SCALE
Keep the rave relatively intimate and illegal.
Approximately 50–100 people total, distributed through several bridge spans.
It should feel big enough to have genuine energy but small enough that someone could realistically organize it secretly underneath this bridge.

a music festival
a warehouse superclub
hundreds of identical background extras
a professional concert stage
barriers
VIP areas
branding
food trucks
festival tents

faintly textured
simple outdoor camping-table character

Create an ultra-macro cinematic close-up from above of a single small mosquito flying around a burning tealight candle at night.
CORE VIEW / ANGLE
The shot is seen from slightly above, looking down diagonally onto the tealight.
Not straight side-on.
Not perfectly top-down.
The perspective should feel like the camera is hovering just above the candle at a steep angle, almost looking directly down onto it from a slightly oblique overhead view.
The tealight must sit on a white plastic table.
The white plastic table surface must be clearly recognizable:
slightly matte
faintly textured
simple outdoor camping-table character
no decoration
no tablecloth
no wood
no metal table
The tealight and the mosquito are the absolute visual center.
CORE SUBJECT
A single small mosquito circles slowly and irregularly around the flame of the tealight.
The mosquito must remain realistically tiny.
Do not enlarge it.
Do not stylize it.
It should feel like a very ordinary mosquito drawn toward the candle flame.
The mosquito moves in tiny arcs, short hesitations and quick unpredictable adjustments around the light.
No perfect orbit.
No swarm.
Only one mosquito.
ULTRA-MACRO FEEL
The shot must feel extremely close.
The candle fills a large portion of the frame.
The mosquito appears small in relation to the candle, but still clearly visible because the camera is so close.
We should feel as if the lens is only a few centimeters above the tealight.
The image should feel intimate, observational and almost scientific in closeness — but still cinematic, not clinical.
FOCUS / DEPTH OF FIELD — CRITICAL
Unlike a very shallow macro look, this shot should have noticeably more depth of field.
Use much deeper focus so that:
the tealight is clearly readable
the flame is clearly readable
the mosquito is clearly readable when flying near the candle
the white plastic tabletop around the candle remains visible and fairly legible
The tealight and mosquito should be in the absolute focus priority.
The focal plane should allow both the candle and the mosquito to feel present and readable together more often.
Still natural and optical, but not excessively shallow.
Do not blur everything except a tiny sliver.
We want a strong macro feeling with more depth and clarity.
TEALIGHT
Use one ordinary small tealight candle in a simple aluminum cup.
No branding.
No decorative holder.
No colored candle.

The metal rim of the tealight should catch warm highlights.
The flame creates a small amber pool of light on the white plastic table surface.
MOSQUITO DETAIL
The mosquito should be realistically rendered:
delicate wings
thin legs
narrow body
tiny antennae
natural proportions

When it passes closest to the flame, its wings may catch the warm light.
Do not freeze it like a specimen.
A tiny amount of wing motion softness is acceptable and desirable.

The tealight sits on the white plastic table and occupies the main central area of the frame.
The camera looks down from a steep oblique top angle.
The mosquito moves around the upper area of the flame and around the candle’s warm halo.
Allow some of the white plastic tabletop to remain visible around the tealight so the surface context is clear.
The composition should feel minimal and raw.
No clutter.
No unnecessary objects.
No people.
No hands.
Just:
white plastic table
tealight
mosquito
night darkness around it

The tealight flame is the main visible light source in the frame.
Warm amber / nicotine-yellow flame around 2200–2700K.

the candle rim
the melted wax

the nearby white plastic table surface

faces
facial proportions
skin
hair
body proportions
clothing

accessories
overall styling

Create a tense cinematic frame of Sicko leading Adam quickly through a dense cornfield deep in the middle of the night.
It is the dead of night.
Not dusk.
Not blue hour.
Not dawn.
There is no moon.
There is no moonlight.
The sky above the cornfield is almost completely black.
The entire environment feels isolated, rural, damp and swallowed by darkness.
CHARACTER POSITION — CRITICAL
SICKO IS CLEARLY WALKING IN FRONT OF ADAM.
He leads the way.
Adam follows directly behind him.
They are NOT walking side by side.
Maintain a clear spatial hierarchy:
CAMERA → SICKO → ADAM → DEEP CORNFIELD
Sicko is approximately 1–1.5 meters ahead of Adam.
Sicko is physically closer to the camera and slightly larger in frame.
Adam remains clearly visible behind him.
Do not completely hide Adam behind Sicko.
Sicko may be slightly offset toward one side of the narrow row while Adam appears in the visual gap behind his shoulder, but they are still moving through the same line of travel.
Both men must be clearly identifiable at the same time.
MOVEMENT
They are moving through the field very briskly and purposefully.
Fast walking.
Almost urgent.
But:
NO RUNNING.
NO JOGGING.
Their bodies lean slightly forward from the speed and resistance of the vegetation.
Sicko moves confidently and without hesitation.
Adam follows close behind.
There is a sense that Sicko knows where he is going and Adam is being pulled deeper into the field behind him.
CORNFIELD
The cornfield must look like a real, evenly planted agricultural field.
The structure is highly regular and repetitive.
Straight parallel rows.
Consistent spacing.
Nearly identical plant height.
Uniform density.
The corn is approximately 2–2.5 meters tall.
The repeating rows create subtle geometric depth disappearing into darkness.
Do not make it look wild or randomly overgrown.
Do not create an open forest-like environment.
Do not create a large path.
There is only a very narrow natural space between the planted rows.
The visual impression should be:
order, repetition, pattern, confinement.
CRITICAL LEAF INTERACTION
The space between the rows is tight.
The corn leaves constantly extend into their path.

Both Sicko and Adam must actively use their bare hands and forearms to push vegetation out of their way.

faces
shoulders
chests
arms
hands

The vegetation bends around him.

Adam then has to push through the same vegetation behind him.

Some leaves scrape across their jackets.
Some bend across their shoulders.
One or two leaves can partially cover their faces.
Several leaves pass very close to the camera in the extreme foreground.

Do not make the vegetation politely separate around them.
They are forcing their way through it.
HANDS — CRITICAL
NEITHER MAN IS WEARING GLOVES.

No leather gloves.

thin legs

natural proportions

slightly matte
faintly textured
simple outdoor camping-table character
no decoration

no wood
no metal table
The tealight and the mosquito are the absolute visual center.

A single small mosquito circles slowly and irregularly around the flame of the tealight.
The mosquito must remain realistically tiny.
Do not enlarge it.
Do not stylize it.
It should feel like a very ordinary mosquito drawn toward the candle flame.
The mosquito moves in tiny arcs, short hesitations and quick unpredictable adjustments around the light.
No perfect orbit.
No swarm.
Only one mosquito.
ULTRA-MACRO FEEL
The shot must feel extremely close.
The candle fills a large portion of the frame.
The mosquito appears small in relation to the candle, but still clearly visible because the camera is so close.

the tealight is clearly readable
the flame is clearly readable
the mosquito is clearly readable when flying near the candle
the white plastic tabletop around the candle remains visible and fairly legible

The flame creates a small amber pool of light on the white plastic table surface.

delicate wings
thin legs
narrow body
tiny antennae
natural proportions

Do not freeze it like a specimen.
A tiny amount of wing motion softness is acceptable and desirable.

mosquito
night darkness around it

SCENE
Deep night in an isolated cornfield somewhere near the Baltic / northeastern German countryside.
Adam and Sicko are walking together through a narrow improvised path between extremely tall rows of mature corn.
The cornfield must feel huge, dense and almost claustrophobic.
The plants rise approximately 2–2.5 meters high on both sides of them, creating two dark vertical walls that almost swallow the men.
The leaves are broad, slightly torn, wet from nighttime moisture and moving softly in the wind.
Some leaves extend directly into the foreground and pass extremely close to the lens.
The ground beneath them is uneven black agricultural soil mixed with flattened weeds, dry leaves, broken stalks and occasional shallow muddy patches.
Nothing about the field should look picturesque or romantic.
It should feel like a real German agricultural field at 1–2 a.m.:
messy,
damp,
cold,
dark,
slightly hostile,
ordinary in a way that becomes unsettling at night.
ENVIRONMENTAL DEPTH
Build strong physical depth through multiple layers:
large out-of-focus corn leaves almost touching the camera
→ Adam and Sicko walking in the narrow path
→ more rows of corn disappearing into darkness
→ a thin irregular opening of night sky above them
→ extremely distant industrial lights beyond the field.
The rows must create strong repeating vertical and diagonal lines.
The corn itself should visually reinforce the film's recurring idea of pattern and repetition — hundreds of nearly identical stalks continuing beyond what the eye can see — but this must remain completely natural and never feel symbolically staged.
The world around them should feel much larger than the characters.
This sequence should visually connect to the film's northern German provincial-noir world: grounded, earthy, dark, understated, with dry realism rather than horror stylization.
NIGHT SKY
Almost no moonlight.
The sky above the corn is very dark blue-black with subtle cloud texture.
Because the corn is so high, the viewer sees only fragments of sky between the leaves.
Occasionally the wind moves the plants enough to briefly reveal a larger patch of sky.
No dramatic full moon.
No fantasy starscape.
No supernatural lighting.
DISTANT RAVE FORESHADOWING
The rave itself should NOT yet be visible.
Only extremely subtle signs suggest that something exists beyond the field.
Far above the corn in the distance, barely visible:
a few tiny red aviation warning lights from an industrial structure,
perhaps one weak sodium-orange glow close to the horizon,
and extremely faint intermittent dirty white or desaturated red light contamination somewhere behind the plants.
Nothing should resemble colorful festival lighting yet.
No lasers.
No neon.
No obvious stage.
No visible crowd.
The viewer should feel that Adam and Sicko are walking toward something, without fully understanding what it is.
ADAM AND SICKO
They walk side by side but cannot always remain perfectly next to each other because the path is narrow.
Sometimes Sicko walks half a step ahead.
Sometimes Adam catches up.
Corn leaves occasionally brush across their shoulders, jackets and faces.
Their body language should feel loose after several hours of drinking and talking, but not drunk-comedy exaggerated.
There is now an understated familiarity between them.
They are no longer strangers.
Neither man is posing.
Neither looks toward camera.
They move naturally through the field while continuing their conversation.
Sicko should retain his worn, working-class physicality and slightly weakened body.
Adam remains calmer and more self-contained.
Their silhouettes occasionally disappear behind foreground leaves for a fraction of the composition.
LIGHTING
There is no artificial film light visibly placed in the cornfield.
Use extremely weak natural night ambience as the primary source.
Faces may sit slightly underexposed but must retain enough eye and skin information to remain human and readable.
Allow deep blacks between the rows.
Occasional distant industrial or rave spill may produce an almost imperceptible warm or dirty-red contamination on the edges of leaves, but it must remain motivated and subtle.
Do NOT create a clean rim light around the characters.
Do NOT illuminate the entire cornfield.
Darkness should remain an important physical part of the image.
The night palette is:
deep steel blue,
charcoal,
black-green vegetation,
muddy brown soil,
restrained warm skin,
tiny distant nicotine-yellow / industrial-red points.
CAMERA
Use a 35mm Zeiss Super Speed Mk II at approximately T2.0.
Camera positioned slightly below chest height, moving inside the path with them.
The camera should feel like a third person quietly following them into the field.
Human shoulder-camera movement:
slow,
controlled,
slightly imperfect,
small lateral corrections as leaves enter the path.
Never polished gimbal movement.
Never a floating Hollywood tracking shot.
The camera sometimes allows leaves to partially obstruct the lens instead of unnaturally avoiding them.
Strong optical depth separation, but keep the cornfield structurally readable.
The background must not dissolve into artificial bokeh.
Foreground leaves may drift softly out of focus only because they are physically extremely close to the lens.
COMPOSITION
Adam and Sicko should occupy only a moderate portion of the image.
The cornfield is the dominant visual subject.
The frame should constantly communicate how deep they are inside it.
Avoid clean symmetrical rows.
Instead create imperfect agricultural geometry:
stalks leaning inward,
broken leaves crossing the path,
irregular gaps,
mud,
different plant heights,
dark spaces between rows.
The path should occasionally become difficult to distinguish from the surrounding plants.
The audience should have the subtle feeling that if the two men stopped walking, they could disappear completely inside the field.
ATMOSPHERE
Cold night air.
Slight humidity.
A gentle wind moving through thousands of corn leaves at different depths.
Nothing overtly frightening happens.
The tension comes entirely from darkness, scale, repetition and the expectation of whatever exists on the other side of the field.
This is not a horror-movie cornfield.
It is a completely ordinary German cornfield that becomes strange simply because it is enormous, dark and almost empty.
The sequence should feel like a threshold between the intimate campsite conversation and the chaotic rave world ahead.
For a few moments Adam and Sicko are isolated together inside an endless dark pattern of corn before emerging into an entirely different environment.
NEGATIVE LOCK
No horror clichés.
No scarecrow.
No supernatural fog.
No blue Hollywood moonlight.
No giant visible moon.
No fantasy lighting.
No bright flashlights.
No obvious festival lights.
No lasers through the corn.
No neon colors.
No teal-orange grade.
No glossy fashion cinematography.
No clean symmetrical maze.
No perfectly manicured cornfield.
No excessive artificial bokeh.
No HDR.
No digital sharpness.
No dramatic backlight.
No posed walking.
No additional people.
No cars.
No buildings clearly visible yet.
No visible rave crowd.
The final image should feel dark, tactile, humid, rural and quietly ominous — two men disappearing into a massive field of repeating vertical lines, with only the faintest suggestion that somewhere beyond the corn another world is waiting.

It leans down and takes one small sip of water from the pool. It lifts its head slightly upward in the natural bird-like swallowing motion, allowing the water to run into its throat.

For a brief moment, it naturally looks around its surroundings — one or two subtle head movements, alert but calm, as if casually checking the environment. No exaggerated twitching, no nervous behavior, no prolonged scanning.
Then it leans down again and takes one second and final small sip of water. Again, it lifts its head slightly to swallow.

No reframing.
No zoom.
No hidden edits.
No angle changes.
The frame remains locked the entire time.
The camera is placed outside the caravan and observes the caravan wall straight on, using the attached caravan-door image as the core framing reference.
This is a simple, bold action built around:
the caravan door suddenly slamming open → the man stepping out casually with a six-pack of canned beer → a small final gesture with the beer and a slight head tilt.
NO MUSIC.
Use only natural sound: subdued outdoor ambience, faint wind, the sharp impact of the caravan door flying open and hitting the outer wall, light movement of clothing, footsteps, and the subtle metallic clink of the beer cans in the six-pack.

window placement
proportions

facial proportions

The window beside it remains visible.

ACTION
At first, nothing happens for a very short beat.
Then the caravan door suddenly flies open hard.
It should feel forceful and abrupt.
The door swings outward with energy and slams against the caravan wall.
The impact should feel physical and loud.
The door must not open gently.
It must not drift open softly.
It must bang open in a sharp, satisfying way.
Immediately after this, the man steps out of the caravan.
He emerges casually and without hurry.
He does not burst out aggressively.
He does not stumble.
He does not look panicked.
He simply comes out with relaxed confidence, as if he knows exactly where he is going and is completely at ease.
He is holding a six-pack of canned beer in one bare hand.
The six-pack must clearly be made up of the beer from reference 2.
The cans should move naturally and give off a slight metallic clink as he steps out.
His bare hand holding the six-pack must remain:
WITHOUT GLOVE.
WITHOUT HAND TATTOOS.
WITHOUT FINGER TATTOOS.
WITHOUT RINGS.

relaxed
easygoing
slightly cool
casual
self-contained
naturally confident

pose like a fashion model

Relaxed.
Almost like a wordless:

or

The important visual element is the water:

SHOT:

The camera looks more frontally toward the hanging string of colored pavilion lights, not strongly from the side and not too diagonal. One or two bulbs are in crisp focus near the center or slightly off-center, while the other bulbs fall off softly into optical blur. The colored bulbs — red, yellow, green and blue — should feel cheap, slightly worn and imperfect, with subtle dirt, tiny scratches, and a weak practical glow. The lights are not festive or overly bright; they are dim, slightly murky, and feel like old campsite decoration.
Thin cigarette smoke drifts upward through the frame, visible mainly where it catches the colored practical light. The smoke should be delicate, layered, and organic — light wisps and curls, not dense fog. It should create a soft veil in front of and between the bulbs, helping the frame feel still, nocturnal and slightly intoxicated.
The background is almost completely dark. Only very faint, soft hints of the pavilion structure may remain visible — perhaps a roof edge, a support pole, or a vague fragment of the campsite beyond — but everything except the lights and smoke stays deeply secondary.
If any human presence is suggested at all, it should be extremely subtle and out of focus, maybe only as a dark shape low in frame. No readable faces. No active interaction. No object in the frame should compete with the lampions.
The image should feel like a pure mood frame: late-night stillness, cigarettes, conversation residue, and quiet melancholy. The shot is less about narrative information and more about atmosphere.
Keep the image tactile, analog and observational. Slight handheld micro-drift is okay, but the frame should overall feel still and controlled. The practical bulbs should bloom gently with restrained halation on the 500T stock.
No bright party feeling, no clean decorative look, no Christmas aesthetic, no nightclub vibe, no excessive fog, no heavy neon glow, no glossy ad lighting, no surreal color intensity, no synthetic blur.

A man rediscovering warmth rather than suddenly becoming happy.

The pose feels caught rather than posed.

The background remains very dark, but it has multiple subtle depth planes.
Behind him, barely visible in shadow:
distant vertical wall structures
vague doorway or corridor openings
one or two dark architectural edges
soft patches of reflected light on a far wall
subtle atmospheric haze separating foreground, middle ground and background
Nothing in the background should compete with the character.
The room should feel large, empty and several meters deep, rather than like a black studio backdrop.
Use strong perspective recession.
Allow faint silhouettes of architecture to disappear gradually into darkness.
A very weak practical light far in the background may create one small, soft pool of dirty tungsten light, heavily underexposed.
The background must remain recognizable enough to create depth, but still 80–90% darkness.
No obvious set decoration.
No bright objects.
No neon.
No visible lamps pointing toward camera.
No artificial bokeh balls.
The depth should come from real spatial layering, light falloff and perspective, not excessive blur.
LIGHTING
Extremely restrained low-key cinematography.
A weak side light catches fragments of:
one side of his face
the sunglasses
strands of hair
leather texture
neck
chest tattoos
gold chain
The foreground subject is slightly brighter than the environment, while light rapidly falls off behind him.
Use negative fill and deep blacks.

RIGHT:

Adam is completely relaxed.
Loose.
Easygoing.
Natural.

Human height.
Natural perspective.
Measured.
Observational.

LIGHTING — PRIMARY PRIORITY
The entire scene is illuminated almost exclusively by cheap practical campsite lights hanging underneath the awning.
A single bright warm-white tungsten bulb hangs slightly above and between the two men and acts as the main motivated light source. It should feel like an ordinary exposed campsite bulb, approximately 2700K–3000K, not like professional film lighting.
This bulb creates a small localized pool of warm light around the plastic table and the two men, while everything beyond the awning quickly falls into darkness.
The light is imperfect and slightly harsh:
visible forehead texture
wrinkles and pores clearly preserved
subtle shine from alcohol, rain and humidity
deep eye sockets
irregular shadows around noses, cheeks and necks
faces slightly underexposed rather than beautifully illuminated
There is NO soft beauty key and NO studio fill.
The side of each face facing away from the practical light falls naturally into deep shadow.
Use subtle negative fill created by the darkness surrounding the awning.
COLORED FESTOON LIGHTS
Across the ceiling of the awning hangs a loose strand of inexpensive old-fashioned campsite party bulbs:
muted red, green, yellow, blue and warm-white bulbs.
They should not flood the entire scene with color.
Instead they create only tiny localized colored accents:
faint green contamination on fabric,
a subtle red reflection,
a tiny blue highlight,
small colored glints on wet surfaces and beer cans.
The dominant illumination on human skin remains dirty warm tungsten, not rainbow lighting.
The colored bulbs should feel slightly tacky, nostalgic and provincial — cheap German campsite decoration that has probably been hanging there for years.
NIGHT / RAIN CONTRAST
Outside the awning is a cold, extremely dark rainy campsite night.
The background should sit several stops darker than the men.
Very faint steel-blue / gray-blue ambient night light separates distant caravans and wet grass from complete blackness, but nothing outside should look artificially illuminated.
Heavy rain is clearly visible only where individual raindrops pass through the warm practical light spilling beyond the awning.
The rain becomes glowing thin streaks close to the light and disappears almost completely once it enters the darkness.
Wet surfaces subtly catch the practical lights:
plastic table
aluminum beer cans
glasses
caravan surfaces
wet ground
Reflections must remain restrained and realistic, never glossy or commercial.
TABLE LIGHT
The pale plastic camping table acts as a weak natural bounce source.
Warm light from the overhead bulb hits the table and creates a very subtle dirty upward bounce onto the men's hands, jaws and lower faces.
Do NOT introduce an additional fill source.
The table should appear brighter than the surrounding campsite but slightly stained, worn and imperfect.
Beer cans and glasses catch small sharp practical highlights.
EXPOSURE
Expose primarily for the men's faces and the central practical bulb.
Allow the bulb itself to approach gentle overexposure with soft filmic halation around the brightest practicals.
Do not recover every shadow.
Large sections of the frame should remain dark.
The emotional impression should be:
two men several beers too deep, isolated inside a tiny warm island of light while cold rain and darkness surround them.

tiny saturated colored bulbs,

Create a highly cinematic exterior shot of a dirty East German rave beneath a massive motorway bridge, seen from outside the crowd, with a slightly blurry, dizzy, intoxicated feeling — as if the viewer has stepped away for a moment, turned around, and is looking back at the scene while already deep in the night.
CORE GEOGRAPHY
The spatial layout must be very clear:
one side: an ugly industrial facility, almost completely dark
center under the bridge: the rave
other side: a dense cornfield
foreground: a low rough concrete wall with beer cans placed on it
This is important:
the shot should feel like the camera is standing outside the rave, at the edge of the location, not inside the crowd.
COMPOSITION — 60 / 30 / 10
Build the image with a clear 60-30-10 composition logic:
60% = WORLD / ARCHITECTURE / ATMOSPHERE
The majority of the image is the massive bridge structure, the oppressive space beneath it, the dark sky fragments, the repeating concrete pillars, the wet ground, and the bleak edge-of-nowhere environment.
The motorway should dominate the frame and feel monumental.
The bridge ceiling presses down across the image with huge concrete beams and dark negative space.
30% = THE RAVE
The rave sits in the middle distance as the visual energy center:
a relatively small but dense cluster of people beneath the bridge, red light, speakers, smoke, and bodies.
It should feel like a hidden feverish pocket beneath overwhelming infrastructure.
10% = FOREGROUND DETAIL
In the near foreground there is a dirty low concrete wall or barrier.
On top of it sit several beer cans:
cheap lager cans
some upright
some dented
maybe one tipped over
wet with condensation
catching red highlights and tiny reflections
These cans act as the foreground anchor and help sell the feeling that the viewer is standing just outside the action.
They should not dominate the whole frame, but they should be clearly visible and add realism, grime, and lived-in atmosphere.
CAMERA / FRAMING
Use a much stronger wide-angle cinematic composition.
Very wide lens feeling, but still grounded and believable:
24mm–28mm equivalent, no fisheye.
The camera is positioned a little low, just behind or beside the wall with the beer cans, looking toward the rave beneath the bridge.
The frame should have:
strong foreground / midground / background depth
dramatic wide-angle spatial expansion
big perspective lines
towering pillars
the motorway structure stretching aggressively overhead
the rave glowing in the distance
cornfield visible to one side
industrial plant faintly visible on the other
This should feel like absolute cinema:
huge scale, strong depth, strong perspective, emotional atmosphere.
Do not make it a flat eye-level photo.
DEPTH OF FIELD / TIEFENSCHÄRFE
The image should have noticeable depth and layered focus, not creamy blur everywhere.
Important:
the beer cans in the foreground should be readable
the rave in the middle distance should also remain recognizable
the architecture in the background should stay legible
Use deep enough depth of field that the whole spatial world can be felt.
At the same time, perception should still feel slightly soft and unstable, as if the viewer’s eyes are not perfectly locking in.
So the look is:
not crisp documentary sharpness
not shallow-focus blur
rather a slightly intoxicated wide-angle image with cinematic depth
INTOXICATED EXTERIOR FEELING
The camera is outside the scene, but the viewer is already in a mildly intoxicated state.
The image should feel:
slightly dizzy
slightly soft
subtly unfixed
visually overstimulated
damp
nocturnal
disoriented but still real
Use restrained perceptual imperfections:
gentle overall softness
slight bloom around red lights
organic red halation
mild motion smear in a few bodies
faint ghosting around bright light sources
light condensation or haze near the lens
tiny veiling flare
slight focus instability
some parts of the frame feeling a touch less stable than others
But:
do not make it psychedelic
do not distort the architecture
do not use fantasy visuals
This is more like:
drunk / exhausted / raving-too-long perception at 3 AM.
LIGHTING
The red floor lights are the key motif.
At the bases of the concrete pillars sit rough portable red uplights that shine straight upward, washing the pillars in intense vertical red.
These red lights travel far up the concrete and partially catch the underside of the bridge.
The result:
red glowing pillars
red spill on wet ground
red glow in haze and smoke
red reflections in puddles
red edges on people and objects
faint red highlights on the beer cans in the foreground
The red should feel:
dirty
practical
strong
cinematic
slightly uneven
not polished like a big event production

The industrial facility on one side should remain mostly dark and ugly.

tanks
chimneys
utility buildings
maybe one or two weak sodium lamps
tiny warning lights
faint smoke or steam

CORNFIELD SIDE
On the opposite side of the rave:
a dense mature cornfield begins almost immediately.
The corn forms a dark wall.
Only the first rows catch bits of red light.
Deeper into the field it becomes nearly black.
The cornfield should help make the place feel enclosed and strange.

dense but not enormous crowd

bottles

wet gravel
mud
puddles
dirt
oily reflections

Use a wide environmental focal length with strong perspective and real spatial depth.
Low saturation overall except for the deep red practical lights.
Steel-blue / gray-green darkness.
Soft highlight roll-off.
Slightly lifted blacks.
Authentic film grain.
Subtle halation.
No digital crispness.
No glossy finish.

The ugly industrial plant dies into darkness on one side, the cornfield swallows the other.

ANTI-STATIC CINEMATIC LOCK — PASTE BEFORE EVERY SHOT
Use the supplied references with these exact roles:

References 2 and 3 = Sicko exact facial identity
Reference 4 = Sicko full body, outfit and proportions
Reference 5 = exact beer-can design
References 6, 7 and 8 = Adam exact facial identity, mullet, sunglasses, tattoos and styling
Reference 9 = exact awning, table and chair setup
Reference 10 = wider campsite continuity and sky / environment context
This is always the exact same campsite pitch, the exact same awning, the exact same plastic table, the exact same chairs and the exact same two men. Do not redesign or relocate anything.
This sequence spans roughly three hours, from around 17:00 on an overcast gray afternoon to full darkness later that evening. Every new frame should feel clearly later in time and several beers further into the conversation.
IMPORTANT:
Do NOT generate static, centered, symmetrical table coverage.
Do NOT default to a clean front-on wide shot.
Do NOT make the scene feel staged like theatre coverage.
Do NOT keep both men fully readable in every frame.
Do NOT make every shot a safe dialogue shot.
Instead:
Use aggressive foreground layers.
Use partial obstruction.
Use lens proximity.
Use macro inserts.
Use shallow optical separation with recognizable environment.
Use asymmetry.
Use strange but believable observational angles.
Use near/far subject layering.
Use partial faces, shoulders, cans, foil and table edges as framing devices.
The camera should feel physically present at the table and increasingly invasive as the evening progresses.
Across the sequence, include several kinds of cinematic framing:
shooting through the clear awning foil
shooting through beer cans
extreme table-level angles
close side angles
partial over-shoulders that do NOT look like TV coverage
very close handheld-feeling two-shots
macro inserts of hands, cigarette, condensation, ring pull, can rim, ashtray, knuckles, lips, eyes, table texture
The awning foil must sometimes appear as a real physical foreground layer with smudges, reflections, creases, droplets, condensation and slight distortion.
The beer progression must clearly escalate shot to shot:
start with 2–3 cans, later 5–7, later 8–12, later 13+.
Add condensation rings, ashtray buildup and small spills gradually, but never turn the table into an absurd garbage heap.

Create a cinematic exterior view of the East German rave from outside the gathering, looking toward the rave beneath the motorway bridge.
The camera is not inside the crowd. It stands roughly 20–40 meters away, somewhere at the dirty edge of the location, observing the entire strange environment from outside.
The geography remains clearly readable:
LEFT: almost completely dark, ugly East German industrial facility
CENTER: rave squeezed beneath the massive motorway bridge
RIGHT: dense black cornfield beginning directly beside the rave
Huge concrete bridge pillars frame the rave in the center. Small red floor lights at their bases throw intense vertical red washes high up the dirty concrete columns and onto fragments of the underside of the motorway.
The industrial plant should remain almost completely dark — only a few weak sodium lamps, tiny warning lights, silhouettes of pipes, tanks, fences and chimneys.
The cornfield forms a dense dark wall on the opposite side. Only the first rows catch occasional red spill.
INTOXICATED EXTERIOR PERCEPTION
The entire image should feel as though you have stepped away from the rave for a moment after already being there for hours.
You look back at it from outside and reality feels slightly unstable.
The rave itself remains recognizable, but perception is beginning to blur.
Use subtle, photographic intoxication effects:
slight overall softness
imperfect focus, as if the eyes struggle to lock onto one distance
soft blooming around the strongest red lights
stronger organic red halation
very subtle motion smear around moving people
faint double-image / ghosting only around a few bright lights and moving silhouettes
slight veiling flare
tiny chromatic separation around extremely bright red highlights
moisture or condensation close to the lens
occasional soft foreground blur
gentle uneven exposure around bright red lights
distant figures becoming indistinct shapes
The effect should be dizzy and blurry, but still cinematic and believable.
Do not make the architecture warped.
Do not turn it into psychedelic imagery.
The feeling should be closer to drunken / intoxicated eyesight at 3 AM than an LSD hallucination.
COMPOSITION
Use a particularly strong cinematic exterior angle.
35mm environmental wide.
Camera positioned low and slightly off-axis.
A dark piece of concrete barrier, wet vegetation, fencing or a few corn leaves can partially obscure the extreme foreground, making it feel like the viewer has wandered away from the party and turned around.
The rave glows deeper underneath the bridge.
The enormous black motorway structure occupies much of the upper frame and compresses everything beneath it.
Red pillars repeat into the distance.
The crowd should appear as a dense but relatively small collection of dark bodies in the middle distance rather than individually staged people.
Wet ground between camera and rave catches fragmented red reflections.
The image should have a strong sense of distance and separation:
the viewer is outside the rave now, but the light and noise still seem to pull them back toward it.
LIGHTING
The red bridge uplights dominate the scene.
Deep saturated red rises vertically along stained concrete pillars.
The rave itself is mostly darkness, silhouettes, smoke and dirty red light.
Almost no blue festival lights.
No colorful lasers.
No polished light show.
Beyond the bridge everything falls rapidly into blackness.
The industrial facility is barely visible.
The cornfield is almost black.

bombers

Grounded 35mm European crime-drama realism.

No perfect composition.

one side: a bleak industrial facility, almost completely dark
center beneath the bridge: the rave
other side: a dense mature cornfield

The red lights are the visual signature of the scene.
Place several small, rough red floor lights directly at the bases of the huge concrete bridge pillars.

The red should feel:
deep
dirty
saturated
dramatic
practical
slightly uneven
not polished or perfectly designed
The concrete catches the red light differently depending on stains, moisture, cracks and texture.
Some pillars are strongly illuminated red at their base and gradually disappear into darkness higher up.
The underside of the motorway should occasionally catch faint red spill, creating huge dark-red architectural planes overhead.
The effect should make the bridge feel massive, oppressive and almost cathedral-like, while still remaining completely believable as an improvised rave setup.
IMPORTANT:
The red lighting is not neon cyberpunk lighting.
It comes from simple portable floor lights / industrial uplights placed on the ground by the ravers.
No elaborate lighting rig.
No giant truss.
No festival production.
INDUSTRIAL PARK
On one side of the bridge is an ugly East German industrial park, but it should be almost completely unlit.
Do not brightly illuminate the factory.
It exists primarily as a dark silhouette and background texture.
Visible only through tiny fragments:
dark warehouses
storage tanks
pipes
metal fencing
chimneys
old industrial structures
small warning lights
perhaps one or two weak dirty sodium lamps
faint steam or smoke barely visible against the night sky
About 80–90% of the industrial park remains dark.
It should feel dead, functional, bleak and unattractive.
No beautiful glowing refinery.
No Blade Runner atmosphere.
The rave lighting under the bridge should be significantly brighter and more visually dominant than the industrial complex.

The rave happens in a relatively small compressed area directly beneath the bridge.

30–60 people
small clusters of people standing, smoking and talking
some dancing closer to the sound system
old speaker stacks
battered flight cases
loose cables on wet ground
generator
dirty folding tables
crates
beer bottles
cigarette butts
trash
cheap plastic cups
old vans and battered German cars partially visible at the edges
No stage.
No DJ superstar setup.
The DJ / sound source can be slightly hidden between speakers and equipment.
The rave should feel like someone found this place and brought speakers and lights there, not like an organized event company constructed it.
People wear:
worn hoodies
bomber jackets
old track jackets
workwear
puffers
dark jeans
cargo pants
beanies
dirty sneakers and boots
Nothing should look fashion-styled.

Immediately on the opposite side of the rave is a dense mature cornfield.
It begins only a few meters away from the bridge pillars.
The tall corn forms almost a dark wall, contributing strongly to the sense of enclosure.
Some red light from the rave catches the outermost rows:
individual leaves glow dark red along their edges
deeper inside the field everything disappears into blackness
wet corn leaves reflect tiny highlights
some stalks lean toward the rave area

You could walk ten steps away from the speakers and disappear completely inside it.

Do not make the location feel large and open.
The rave occupies a tight corridor beneath the motorway.
Above:
the enormous dark concrete ceiling.
One side:
the nearly black industrial park behind fencing and walls.

the dense cornfield.
Around:
massive bridge pillars.

Use a low, slightly off-axis 35mm perspective, as though the camera is standing among the people at the edge of the rave.

The camera looks past it deeper underneath the bridge toward the gathering.
Another pillar further away is also illuminated red, creating repeating vertical red shapes disappearing into the distance.
The bridge decks above create aggressive diagonal lines across the frame.

speaker
parked car
person in foreground
corn leaves

side layer: dark cornfield

large raw concrete pillars
heavy bridge beams overhead

a few people gathering in small groups

a restrained underground energy

tall dark corn stalks

specific
cinematic
slightly claustrophobic
damp
nocturnal

the crowd and vehicle setup placed deeper in the frame

asymmetrical framing
layered perspective
partial occlusion from a pillar or corn stalks

No glossy EDM look.

The pull tab is still flat.
The can is completely unopened.

faded tattoos
cigarette tattoo
heart-and-arrow “OMA”
small crude finger tattoos
wrinkles
veins
dry skin
slightly dirty fingernails
realistic age spots and imperfections

Adam sits directly around that same corner, approximately one seat-width away.
They are close to each other.
They are NOT sitting opposite each other.
Because the camera is attached to the Sick Man’s beer, we look diagonally past the beer rim and fingers toward Adam around the table corner.
The converging table edges should subtly reveal the 90-degree seating arrangement.

muted undershirt

→ diagonal table corner
→ Adam softly visible just beyond
→ Adam’s second can

Choose a bold variant such as:
lens directly beside the pull tab, only 2–3 cm above the lid
lens almost flush with the metal rim, looking outward underneath the approaching fingers
camera slightly tilted with the circular rim cutting diagonally across the bottom of frame

camera placed behind the pull tab so the tab becomes a huge sharp foreground silhouette

highly asymmetric frame with only a fragment of the can lid visible in one corner while the fingers dominate the opposite side

Both protagonists are large in the foreground, close to camera.
They sit together at the cheap campsite table after a long night of drinking.
The composition should feel intimate, slightly confrontational and strange.
Do NOT create a conventional balanced two-shot.
Instead:
Adam occupies the right foreground
Sicko occupies the center-left foreground
the huge title dominates the left and upper background
the campsite table enters across the bottom foreground
the scratch card sits prominently on the table between them
Both characters should feel very close to the viewer.
ADAM
Use the supplied Adam reference images for his exact identity.
Preserve:
exact facial identity
same age
same facial structure
washed dusty-pink bucket hat
dark jacket
subtle gold chain
tired charismatic presence
slightly detached expression
dark hair
natural skin texture
He is immortal but must NOT look supernatural.
No hand tattoos.
Adam looks tired, curious and emotionally unreadable.
He is leaning toward the table, looking toward the scratch card or camera.
SICKO
Use the supplied Sicko references for his exact identity.
Preserve:
exact face
age
hair
weathered skin
gaunt body
exhausted but warm expression
his exact clothing
tattooed hands if visible
He looks physically ill and deeply worn down, but still alive, charismatic and human.
Do NOT make him grotesque.
Do NOT make him look like a zombie.
Sicko sits close beside Adam, leaning slightly toward the scratch card.
Their proximity should suggest they have already been talking and drinking together for hours.
THE TABLE
The table must be clearly visible in the foreground.
Use an old cheap plastic camping table matching the campsite references.
On the table place:
the beer from the supplied reference images
multiple matching beer cans / bottles
one opened beer prominently near Sicko
another beer clearly visible near Adam
additional empty or half-empty beers suggesting a long drinking session
cigarette ash / ashtray
small traces of the night before
coins
the scratch card
The beer must be PROMINENT AND CLEARLY VISIBLE.
Use the exact visual design of the beer from the supplied references:
same packaging,
same colors,
same general can/bottle appearance.
Do not invent a completely different beer design.
However, the beer should still feel naturally placed on the table rather than presented like a product advertisement.
The table should communicate:
these two men have been drinking together for hours.
SCRATCH CARD / RUBBELLOS
The scratch card is a major visual storytelling object.
Place a worn physical scratch card prominently in the lower foreground, lying on the table or slightly tilted toward camera.
It should contain a clear 3x3 field structure.
The icon language of the fields is based on the supplied symbolic reference:
SYMBOL 1
A single heavy old iron nail.
SYMBOL 2
An infinity symbol constructed from twisted barbed wire.
These two symbols are the core graphic language of the scratch card.
The infinity symbol should be simple and immediately recognizable:
∞
but constructed physically from dark twisted barbed wire.
The nails should look like old hand-forged iron nails:
heavy,
rough,
slightly oxidized,
graphic,
iconic.
Several fields have already been scratched open.
Some reveal nails.
Some reveal barbed-wire infinity symbols.
One final field should remain partly or completely covered with silver scratch material.
This unresolved field should subtly become the conceptual focus.
Do NOT make the scratch card look like a colorful modern lottery advertisement.
It should look old, cheap, slightly dirty, faded and believable.
SCRATCH-CARD TEXTURE ACROSS THE POSTER
Subtly extend the Rubbellos concept into the entire poster.
Parts of the background or typography can look slightly:
scratched
rubbed
abraded
partially revealed
covered by thin remnants of silver-gray coating
But keep this controlled.
The poster should not become visually messy.
The title must remain perfectly readable.
COLOR WORLD
Main background:
deep dirty petrol green / oxidized dark teal
Main typography:
dusty salmon / faded coral / dirty washed pink
Scratch material:
aged silver-gray
Human skin:
natural, slightly warm, tired, realistic
Small practical accents:
nicotine yellow,
dirty cream,
faded beer-label colors
Very strong graphic separation between dark petrol and coral typography.
Muted rather than neon.
CAMPSITE BACKGROUND
Behind the characters, subtly show the world of the film:
old German caravan
damp campsite
wet gray-green grass
plastic chairs
cheap campsite furniture
coastal overcast atmosphere
cold northern European sky
The campsite must remain recognizable but simplified.
Do NOT let background detail compete with the title and characters.
No American trailer park.
No Western atmosphere.
No desert.
No luxury camping.
It should unmistakably feel like a modest German Baltic / North German campsite.

Grounded European 35mm crime-drama realism.
ARRICAM LT

Kodak Vision3 500T 5219 rated at EI 320

Real skin texture:

wrinkles

moisture
uneven pigmentation
real human imperfections
No glossy AI skin.

The finished image should look like a real vintage physical poster or giant old scratch card that has survived years of handling.

The physical wear should feel authentic and random.

Not action.

strange
human

SPATIAL GEOMETRY — CRITICAL
Both men are sitting at the SAME CORNER of the rectangular table.
They are not opposite each other.
They sit on the two adjacent sides that meet at one single table corner, forming a clear 90-degree L-shape.
Adam sits on one side of the corner.
The tattooed Sick Man sits immediately around the same corner, 90 degrees to Adam’s right.
They are therefore relatively close to each other, sharing the same corner of the table.
The camera should clearly communicate this geometry through the visible table edges:
one table edge leads toward Adam, the second table edge leads toward the Sick Man, and both edges meet at the same corner between them.
The shot should feel intimate because the two men are seated close around this one corner.
EXTREME MACRO FOREGROUND
The camera is positioned extremely close to the Sick Man’s hands.
His tattooed hands and beer can dominate the foreground.
One rough older hand grips a closed pale aluminum beer can.
His second hand is already reaching toward the pull tab, thumb and index finger almost hooking underneath it.
Capture the exact instant before the can cracks open.
The tab remains flat.
The beer is still fully closed.
Push very close:
pull tab
metal rim
condensation
tiny scratches
fingertips
tattooed skin
wrinkles
pores
fingernails
should carry most of the image.
Do not show excessive empty table.
TATTOOED HANDS
Older German working-class male hands:
weathered skin
visible veins
fine wrinkles
slightly reddish tone
dry texture
imperfect nails
natural age spots
Use aged, faded tattoo language:
cigarette tattoo
heart-and-arrow with “OMA”
simple crude finger symbols
The tattoos should look old and naturally embedded into the skin, never fresh or graphic.
ADAM — CLOSE AROUND THE SAME CORNER
Adam is seated very near the Sick Man, directly around the same table corner.
He appears in the background / midground, diagonally offset from the Sick Man rather than far across the table.
Adam should feel only approximately one seat-width away, not several meters distant.
He is softly out of focus but recognizable:
dark messy hair
narrow black wraparound sunglasses
dark worn jacket
muted undershirt
Adam also holds his own closed pale beer can.
His can has:
no readable label, no visible logo, no identifiable branding.
His free hand may already be moving toward his own pull tab, subtly mirroring the Sick Man.
The composition should clearly prepare the next action:
both men crack their beers almost simultaneously, then move their cans only a short distance across the shared table corner to clink them together.
DYNAMIC CAMERA ANGLE
Do not create a conventional frontal two-shot.
Use a bold macro perspective such as:
camera almost touching the Sick Man’s can, looking diagonally across the shared table corner toward Adam
camera at pull-tab height with Adam appearing blurred just beyond the corner
strong three-quarter macro angle, one table edge running diagonally through frame
camera very close behind one tattooed hand, Adam framed through the gap between hand and can
subtle Dutch angle that makes the two converging table edges visually dynamic
extreme off-center framing, foreground can huge on one side while Adam occupies the opposite background third
The table corner itself should become part of the composition, visually connecting both men.
VISUAL LINE
Build the image around this directional flow:
tattooed hand → foreground can → table corner → Adam → Adam’s second can
The viewer should immediately understand that both men belong to the same intimate action around one corner.
DEPTH OF FIELD
Very strong natural optical depth separation.
Sharpest:
foreground pull tab and fingers
Then:
tattooed hand and can
Then:
Adam and his can softly readable
Then:
pavilion environment dissolving into depth
Adam should remain identifiable, but never compete with the foreground can.
ENVIRONMENT
Only vague atmospheric hints of:
white plastic table
translucent pavilion walls
caravans outside
wet grass
muddy campsite
overcast grey sky
Keep the environment heavily softened.
Cool northern-European daylight, slightly underexposed, damp and lived-in.
HARD NEGATIVES
No men sitting opposite each other.
No long distance between the characters.
No Adam directly across the table.
No separate table corners.
No symmetrical face-to-face composition.
No beer can lying on the table.
No opened cans.
No foam.
No spray.
No readable branding.
No extra people.
No extra hands.
No malformed fingers.
No glossy beer-commercial aesthetic.
No sterile product photography.
FINAL REQUIREMENT: both men sit immediately around the SAME table corner on two adjacent sides of the table, forming a clear 90-degree L-shape. The Sick Man’s tattooed hands and unopened beer dominate the extreme macro foreground, while Adam sits close around that same corner in soft focus holding his own unopened unlabeled beer, ready for both cans to be opened and clinked together in the next moment.

blue parked car → open parking gap → old man’s left pavilion / awning
The arriving car enters that exact gap.
It must NOT park in the central lane.
It must NOT park on the right side.
It must NOT park directly in front of the old man.
It must NOT continue behind unrelated caravans.
The car turns left from the campsite lane and pulls into the available space between the blue car and the outside edge of the old man’s pavilion.

This bulb creates a small localized pool of warm light around the plastic table and the two men, while everything beyond the awning quickly falls into darkness.
The light is imperfect and slightly harsh:
visible forehead texture
wrinkles and pores clearly preserved
subtle shine from alcohol, rain and humidity
deep eye sockets
irregular shadows around noses, cheeks and necks
faces slightly underexposed rather than beautifully illuminated
There is NO soft beauty key and NO studio fill.
The side of each face facing away from the practical light falls naturally into deep shadow.
Use subtle negative fill created by the darkness surrounding the awning.

Across the ceiling of the awning hangs a loose strand of inexpensive old-fashioned campsite party bulbs:
muted red, green, yellow, blue and warm-white bulbs.

faint green contamination on fabric,
a subtle red reflection,
a tiny blue highlight,
small colored glints on wet surfaces and beer cans.
The dominant illumination on human skin remains dirty warm tungsten, not rainbow lighting.
The colored bulbs should feel slightly tacky, nostalgic and provincial — cheap German campsite decoration that has probably been hanging there for years.

Heavy rain is clearly visible only where individual raindrops pass through the warm practical light spilling beyond the awning.

plastic table

glasses
caravan surfaces
wet ground

two men several beers too deep, isolated inside a tiny warm island of light while cold rain and darkness surround them.

The camera remains completely locked in the exact starting frame. Adam sits in the foreground exactly as in the source image, watching the football match off-screen. He feels completely detached from the crowd.
At the beginning of the shot, Adam takes one single drag from the cigarette — calm, cool, controlled, without emotional emphasis. Immediately after that, he casually flicks the cigarette away with an effortless, cool gesture. The action should feel natural and understated, not showy. Important: his hands must not have tattoos.
Adam’s face and body language remain unchanged throughout. He reacts zero to what happens in the match. No surprise, no tension, no smile, no irritation, no participation. He stays emotionally blank and separate from everyone around him.
In the background, the spectators are quietly following the game. Then an obvious foul happens somewhere on the pitch outside frame.
The whole stand reacts at once with anger and frustration. Several spectators jerk forward, throw their arms up, or lean out in outrage. One or two stand up abruptly. One man shouts loudly toward the pitch in anger, but the words are not understandable — just a raw, emotional burst of indistinct football yelling.
Important: nobody throws beer.
After this short wave of outrage, the crowd settles back down. The spectators sit back in their seats one after another, still annoyed, still grumbling, still visibly angry about the foul. By the end of the shot, the stand is seated again.
Adam never joins the emotional rhythm of the stadium. While the whole stand briefly rises in collective anger and then settles, he remains completely apart — motionless, numb, observational, untouched.
Tone: authentic lower-league German football atmosphere, grounded, observational, dry, lived-in, never comedic, never overplayed. The core contrast is that the whole stand reacts as one organism, while Adam seems disconnected from all of it.

Create an extreme 90-degree vertical bird’s-eye view directly above an enormous chemical processing plant in the German provinces.

Repeated junctions.

SHOT — CHEMICAL LABYRINTH
Create an extreme 90-degree vertical bird’s-eye view directly above an enormous chemical processing plant in the German provinces.
The camera looks perfectly straight down. No horizon. No sky. The industrial complex fills almost the entire frame.
At first glance it must look like a real, aging German chemical works: weathered steel pipelines, cylindrical storage tanks, cooling systems, narrow service roads, concrete structures, rust-stained roofs, maintenance platforms, cable channels, small utility buildings and dense networks of pipes.
But the longer the viewer looks, the more the entire facility should begin to resemble an impossible labyrinth.
Thousands of pipes bend at hard 90-degree angles, run parallel, split, reconnect, double back and disappear beneath other structures. Service paths repeatedly lead toward apparent exits before turning back into the plant. Circular tanks interrupt the rectangular geometry like nodes inside an enormous mechanical brain.
The composition should contain repetition inside repetition.
Rows of nearly identical tanks.
Parallel pipe corridors.
Repeated junctions.
Identical rectangular processing units.
Loops feeding into larger loops.
The architecture remains completely plausible and functional — never fantasy, never surreal machinery — yet from this altitude the accumulated industrial geometry creates an overwhelming visual pattern.
The plant should feel as though it has expanded organically over decades without anyone ever seeing the whole system.
Surrounding the facility, only at the very edges of frame, show traces of German provincial landscape: wet gray roads, narrow fields, dark green tree lines, a few modest detached houses, perhaps a small football pitch or allotment gardens in the distance. The ordinary rural world makes the enormous industrial maze feel even stranger.
HUMAN SCALE
Include several extremely small maintenance workers moving through different parts of the facility.
They should almost disappear inside the structure.
One tiny worker crosses a narrow open concrete section near the center of the labyrinth.
He is heading toward what visually appears to be an exit — but the surrounding pipelines curve around him and eventually return toward the same central system.
Do not make this symbolic in an obvious way.
It should only become apparent after studying the image.
THEMATIC SUBTEXT
The chemical plant represents the hidden pattern beneath human hope:
every path seems new when you are walking through it,
but from far enough above, you can see where all of them lead.
The image should create the disturbing feeling that an individual experiences decisions, progress and hope — while the larger structure endlessly repeats the same movements.
Not hopelessness.
Repetition mistaken for possibility.

Cold overcast northern German daylight after rain.
Wet asphalt and metal surfaces softly reflect the pale sky.
Muted gray-green vegetation.
Steel-blue industrial metal.
Old concrete.
Small traces of faded rust and nicotine-yellow industrial lighting from inside some structures.
A few thin plumes of white steam drifting across sections of the plant, but never enough to obscure the geometry.
No dramatic black smoke.
No sunset.
No orange industrial spectacle.
The atmosphere is quiet, damp and psychologically heavy.

No visible horizon.

No impossible pipes.

No neon.

No HDR.

No clean modern tech campus.
No logos, company names, warning text or recognizable branding.
No giant crowds.

No obvious maze walls.

No sky.

Anthracite pitched roofs and dark roof tiles.
Simple rectangular footprints.
Dark gray window frames.
Small attached garages and carports.
Gray concrete paving stones.
Narrow driveways.
Tiny newly planted hedges.
Young trees supported by wooden stakes.
Gravel front gardens.
Small rectangular lawns.
Terraces with inexpensive outdoor furniture.
Garden sheds.
Trampolines.
Children’s paddling pools.
Raised vegetable beds.
Barbecue grills.
Bicycles leaning against sheds.
Recycling bins lined up beside driveways.

THE PATTERN
The repetition must be immediately striking.
House.
Driveway.
Car.
Garden.
Terrace.
House.
Driveway.
Car.
Garden.
Terrace.
Again.
And again.
And again.

Roads curve through the settlement, branch into cul-de-sacs, reconnect visually and form repeating loops.
Rows of identical dark roofs create rhythmic geometric bands across the image.
Tiny gardens repeat as rectangular green cells.
Cars occupy almost identical positions in adjacent driveways.
Trash bins stand in little groups.
Trampolines appear again and again like repeated circular symbols inside the rectangular grid.
Nothing is perfectly symmetrical.
There are tiny imperfections everywhere.
But from high enough above, all individuality begins to disappear.

The subdivision is inhabited.
Very small human figures should be visible throughout the image, each engaged in ordinary optimistic rituals:

someone planting a young tree,
a couple carrying moving boxes into a house,
a child jumping on a trampoline,
someone washing a newly purchased car,
a family sitting around a small terrace table,
someone installing a fence,
a woman watering newly planted flowers,
two neighbors talking across identical hedges.
Every person is building, maintaining or improving something.
Nobody looks unhappy.
Nobody behaves strangely.
That is essential.
The disturbing quality comes only from the altitude.
At ground level these are individual lives.
From above, they become a pattern.

everyone believes they are building a different future, while from far enough away the futures begin to look the same.

No giant symbols.
No visible maze walls.
No text.
The physical reality itself creates the idea.

Concrete foundations.
Stacks of paving stones.
Bare earth.
Temporary construction fencing.

Muted gray-green lawns.

garden,
car,
trampoline,
terrace,
hedge,

car,

Erstelle eine minimalistische, monochrome Tattoo-/Illustrationsgrafik auf sauberem weißen Hintergrund. Im Zentrum des Bildes befinden sich drei große, dunkle, alte Eisennägel. Der mittlere Nagel steht senkrecht und ist der längste. Die beiden anderen Nägel stehen leicht schräg links und rechts daneben, fächerförmig angeordnet. Alle drei Nägel haben breite, abgenutzte Köpfe oben und lange, spitz zulaufende Enden nach unten. Die Oberfläche der Nägel wirkt rau, metallisch, dunkel, leicht glänzend und abgenutzt.
Um die drei Nägel herum verläuft Stacheldraht in Form eines liegenden Unendlichkeitszeichens (∞). Das Unendlichkeitszeichen soll klar lesbar sein und sich links und rechts symmetrisch um die Nägel ausbreiten. In der Mitte kreuzt sich der Stacheldraht genau vor bzw. zwischen den Nägeln, sodass es wirkt, als seien die Nägel von diesem Draht zusammengehalten oder gebunden. Die Drahtstruktur soll realistisch verdreht sein, mit regelmäßig verteilten scharfen Widerhaken. Der Draht bildet die komplette Infinity-Form, anstatt einer losen, zufälligen Wicklung.
Stil: schwarz-graue, handgezeichnete, gritty Tattoo-Ästhetik, mit charcoal-/ink-artiger Schraffur, leicht rauen Konturen, hohem Kontrast und feinen weißen Lichtreflexen auf dem Metall.
