Strong optical depth separation with Adam sharply resolved and the environment soft but still naturally recognizable — never artificial bokeh. Natural North German coastal daylight, subtle negative fill, no beauty lighting. Muted Baltic palette: cold steel-blue sky, gray-green coastal grass, restrained warm skin, soft highlight roll-off, slightly lifted blacks, low saturation. Medium-fine authentic 35mm grain, subtle halation, tiny organic imperfections, no HDR, no digital crispness, no glossy commercial finish.
REFERENCE LOCK — ADAM: use the supplied Adam reference images as the exact identity AND wardrobe reference. Preserve his exact facial anatomy, age, proportions, hair, skin texture, facial wear, clothing, layering, colors, silhouette, fit and styling. Same washed faded pink bucket hat, same narrow black wraparound sunglasses, same worn dark outer jacket, same light ribbed undershirt, same neck and upper-chest tattoos. Do not redesign, simplify, replace or add any garment or accessory.
SHOT: extremely intimate cinematic close-up of Adam walking along the crest of a North German coastal dike. Adam is positioned DIRECTLY IN THE CENTER OF THE FRAME and dominates the entire composition. Frame approximately from upper chest upward, deliberately showing enough of his neck and upper chest so that the tattoos remain clearly visible.
Camera directly in front of him at eye level, as if slowly tracking backward while he walks toward camera. Observational, unstaged, slightly uncomfortable intimacy.
Adam’s head, shoulders and upper torso physically obscure almost the entire road behind him. Only tiny peripheral fragments of the narrow paved dike road are visible at the extreme LEFT and RIGHT edges beside his shoulders. The road must NOT be visible as a central line behind him. No strong vanishing point. No visible asphalt directly behind his head or torso.
Adam is the absolute visual center. NO HANDS NEAR HIS FACE. Both arms are naturally lowered outside the frame. His neck and upper-chest tattoos are therefore completely unobstructed and clearly visible.
CIGARETTE: a single completely UNLIT cigarette rests loosely between Adam’s lips, slightly toward one corner of his mouth. Nobody is touching it. No hand holding it. No fingers in front of his chin, mouth, neck or chest. The cigarette is clearly unlit: no ember, no glowing tip, no smoke, no ash, no flame, no lighter.
Adam looks tired, weathered, gaunt and emotionally distant. Slightly hollow, sunken cheeks, tired eyes behind the sunglasses, pale lived-in skin, visible pores, under-eye texture, slight stubble, fine lines and tiny imperfections. His expression is detached, quiet and melancholic — not aggressively cool, not posing for fashion photography.
NECK + CHEST TATTOOS: preserve the tattoo placement and visual language from the Adam references precisely. The tattoos should feel aged and naturally embedded in the skin rather than freshly printed. They remain clearly readable because nothing covers his throat or chest. Do not invent additional tattoos.
IMPORTANT: Adam has absolutely NO tattoos on his hands or fingers. If any tiny portion of a hand accidentally enters the bottom edge of the frame, it is completely clean natural skin.
ENVIRONMENT:
LEFT SIDE: a simple weathered public bench is partially visible behind Adam toward the left edge of frame. The bench sits beside the dike road and is softly out of focus. Practical, slightly aged coastal infrastructure, never decorative or modern.
RIGHT SIDE: the sea is clearly visible beyond Adam’s right shoulder. Cold gray-blue North Sea / Baltic water extends toward the horizon. The grassy strip between the road and the sea is SHORT, CLOSE-CROPPED DIKE GRASS. It looks maintained, wind-cut and low to the ground — approximately ankle-height or lower. No tall coastal grass. No reeds. No long wild stalks. No meadow-like vegetation. Nothing should obscure the view of the sea. The right side must feel open, exposed and windswept, with a clean low grassy slope descending toward the water.
BACKGROUND PEOPLE: there are absolutely NO people visible anywhere in the background. The elderly woman on the folding bicycle may logically be somewhere much farther down the road within the story, but Adam’s central body completely blocks that portion of the road from camera. NO cyclist. NO distant silhouette. NO woman in pink. NO pedestrian.
WEATHER + SKY: the weather must clearly suggest that Adam is walking into incoming bad weather. Behind him on the LEFT side of the frame, it is still a little brighter, but no longer fresh or open — the brightness is already dimming. There should be a weak, pale leftover opening in the sky behind him on frame-left: desaturated blue mixed with milky white-gray light, slightly subdued, already darker than a fair-weather sky. It should feel like the last remaining lighter patch after better weather, but that patch is already fading and being closed off. Toward frame-right and increasingly overhead, the clouds become denser, darker and more layered, with a heavier gray storm front building above the sea. The image should clearly read as: behind him it is still somewhat brighter, but it has already darkened and is about to close in completely. He is leaving the last weak brightness behind and moving toward the more oppressive weather ahead. No rain yet, but a strong sense that the sky is tightening.
SKY COMPOSITION: LEFT side of frame = slightly brighter but already dimmed pale blue-gray opening behind him, with thin cloud cover moving in and reducing the light. RIGHT side of frame = darker layered gray-white to gray storm clouds above the sea, visibly heavier and more threatening. [SHOT] Environmental establishing shot of an aging provincial German football stadium near the Baltic coast, somewhere between a forgotten regional-league ground and an oversized municipal sports complex built decades ago. The architecture feels unmistakably Central European and slightly post-industrial: long weathered concrete terraces, rows of dark wet seating, narrow steel handrails, chain-link fencing, old blue-painted barriers with chipped paint, a simple covered grandstand with a heavy corrugated-metal roof, exposed concrete support structure, and tall skeletal floodlight towers rising into a pale overcast sky.
A reddish-brown running track separates the stands from the football pitch. The grass is maintained but imperfect, deep muted green with worn areas near the touchline. Simple dugouts, maintenance gates and utilitarian service structures sit around the edge of the field. No modern LED architecture, no luxury boxes, no polished Bundesliga atmosphere. This is a stadium that has hosted thousands of ordinary Saturday matches, youth tournaments, local derbies and rainy winter fixtures.
The stands are almost completely empty. Evidence of people remains: crushed paper cups, cigarette packets, wet newspapers, plastic food trays, discarded tickets and a few empty beer bottles scattered between the concrete steps. Nothing arranged decoratively; the debris should feel accidental and mundane. Rust stains run beneath bolts and railings. Moss and dark moisture collect in cracks. Paint has faded unevenly after years of Baltic rain, salt air and cold winters.
The stadium should feel strangely too large for the small town surrounding it, as though its best years happened decades ago. Beyond the far stand: fragments of modest residential roofs, industrial sheds, bare trees, utility poles and flat northern-German landscape disappearing beneath a gray horizon. No recognizable club branding, no real sponsors, no readable corporate logos, no famous stadium identifiers.
It is early morning after rain. The concrete is still wet, reflecting small patches of the washed-out sky. Cold diffused daylight, no direct sun. Thin atmospheric moisture in the distance, but absolutely no cinematic fog machine effect. The air should almost feel cold when looking at the image.
Composition inspired by documentary photographs of old European football grounds: camera positioned high on one side of the terraces, looking diagonally across the empty stands toward the pitch so that railings, concrete steps and the roof structure create strong foreground layers. Let the grandstand occupy a substantial part of the frame rather than presenting a symmetrical postcard view. The football pitch appears partially rather than perfectly centered. Include foreground obstruction from railings or structural elements to make the camera feel physically present inside the stadium.
35mm Zeiss Super Speed Mk II, T4. Deep enough focus that the architecture, opposite stand and floodlight towers remain clearly readable while maintaining natural optical depth. Locked-off observational frame with barely perceptible human camera breathing. No dramatic hero composition. No characters posing in the frame. The place itself is the protagonist.
The emotional quality is not “abandoned stadium” horror. It is ordinary, tired, melancholy provincial life: functional, slightly neglected, damp and deeply familiar. A place that is still used, just currently empty. Northern European realism with a subtle sense that something important is about to happen in an otherwise completely unimportant place.

Around the nose: visible pores, mild redness at the nostrils, slight irritation, subtle oiliness, and realistic tonal change into the cheeks.
Cheeks: uneven tone, faint blotchiness, small capillaries in places, shallow pores, slight roughness, and gentle changes between warmer pink-beige and cooler grayish areas.

Lips: dry natural lip texture, small vertical lip lines, slightly uneven pigmentation, soft desaturation, and a believable matte surface - not glossy, not smooth, not overdefined.
Jaw and chin: slightly rougher texture, subtle laxity, irregular pore density, sparse stubble, and more weathered wear.
Neck: thin, age-true skin with vertical tension bands, fine creases, and realistic tonal variation; not sculpted like plastic.
Add real microscopic imperfection without overdoing it: pore size variation, tiny broken capillaries, faint sun damage, mild sallowness in some planes, occasional small freckles or pigment specks, subtle shaving-shadow irregularity, tiny asymmetries in skin folds, and natural tonal patchiness. Use highly realistic skin behavior across different facial zones:

Jaw and chin: slightly rougher texture, subtle laxity, irregular pore density, sparse stubble, and more weathered wear.
Neck: thin, age-true skin with vertical tension bands, fine creases, and realistic tonal variation; not sculpted like plastic.

Around the nose, include visible pore structure, mild redness near the nostril, and natural tonal irregularity. The jaw and chin should feel slightly rougher, with light grey stubble, uneven beard shadow, irregular follicle density, and subtle dryness. The lips should be matte, slightly dry, with fine vertical lines and natural uneven pigmentation. The neck should show thin age-true skin, fine creasing, tendon definition, and realistic tonal variation.

[SHOT] Environmental establishing shot of a small but still active provincial German football stadium near the Baltic coast. The camera stands on the concrete terrace of the home stand, looking diagonally across the pitch and toward the opposite grandstand. The perspective is clearly from the tribune itself: wet concrete steps in the foreground, chipped blue railings, steel handrails, perimeter fencing, and the geometry of the seating terraces leading the eye into the frame.
This is not a lost place and not abandoned. It is an aging lower-league stadium that is still used every week. Capacity around 2,000 spectators, but normally only a few hundred attend matches. The place should feel modest, local and functional rather than dead. Show signs of active use: the grass pitch is maintained and playable, the white field markings are fresh, the running track is worn but intact, the dugouts are functional, the floodlight towers still work, the barriers and gates are in use, and the stadium architecture feels old but operational. The terraces and roofed stand are weathered, with stained concrete, faded paint, rust traces and damp surfaces, but everything still clearly belongs to a working football ground.
Important balance: the stadium should feel tired, cold and melancholy, but still alive in a practical sense. Avoid the impression of decay for decay’s sake. There may be a little everyday litter left from the previous match day — paper cups, a newspaper, cigarette packs, small debris — but only enough to suggest recent use, not neglect. The image should communicate: this place hosted a game recently and will host another one soon.
Architecture: one large covered main stand with a corrugated roof and concrete structure, simple open terraces, blue-painted barriers and railings, tall old floodlight masts, modest club infrastructure, and beyond the stadium modest residential houses, low industrial sheds, bare winter trees and flat northern landscape. The setting should feel unmistakably German regional league, not modern, not glamorous, not iconic.
There must be no people visible anywhere in the frame: no players, no staff, no spectators. The emptiness is temporary, as if the stadium is waiting for the next match. The mood is quiet, overcast, damp and observant, not apocalyptic.
Early morning or gray daytime after rain. Wet steps and concrete catch soft reflections from the pale sky. The air feels cold. Low-saturation steel-blue and gray-green tones dominate. The scene should have the emotional charge of ordinary northern European realism: a place of weekly routine, local history and small crowds, holding a subtle tension because something is about to begin here.
35mm Zeiss Super Speed Mk II, T4. Environmental wide. Readable depth across foreground terrace, pitch and opposite stand. Locked-off or barely breathing frame. No heroic symmetry, no postcard composition, no dramatic spectacle — just a truthful, cinematic observation of a still-active small-town stadium.

[SHOT] Environmental establishing shot of a small but still active provincial German football stadium near the Baltic coast. The camera stands on the concrete terrace of the home stand, looking diagonally across the pitch and toward the opposite grandstand. The perspective is clearly from the tribune itself: wet concrete steps in the foreground, chipped blue railings, steel handrails, perimeter fencing, and the geometry of the seating terraces leading the eye into the frame.
This is not a lost place and not abandoned. It is an aging lower-league stadium that is still used every week. Capacity around 2,000 spectators, but normally only a few hundred attend matches. The place should feel modest, local and functional rather than dead. Show signs of active use: the grass pitch is maintained and playable, the white field markings are fresh, the running track is worn but intact, the dugouts are functional, the floodlight towers still work, the barriers and gates are in use, and the stadium architecture feels old but operational. The terraces and roofed stand are weathered, with stained concrete, faded paint, rust traces and damp surfaces, but everything still clearly belongs to a working football ground.
Important balance: the stadium should feel tired, cold and melancholy, but still alive in a practical sense. Avoid the impression of decay for decay’s sake. There may be a little everyday litter left from the previous match day — paper cups, a newspaper, cigarette packs, small debris — but only enough to suggest recent use, not neglect. The image should communicate: this place hosted a game recently and will host another one soon.
Architecture: one large covered main stand with a corrugated roof and concrete structure, simple open terraces, blue-painted barriers and railings, tall old floodlight masts, modest club infrastructure, and beyond the stadium modest residential houses, low industrial sheds, bare winter trees and flat northern landscape. The setting should feel unmistakably German regional league, not modern, not glamorous, not iconic.
There must be no people visible anywhere in the frame: no players, no staff, no spectators. The emptiness is temporary, as if the stadium is waiting for the next match. The mood is quiet, overcast, damp and observant, not apocalyptic.
Early morning or gray daytime after rain. Wet steps and concrete catch soft reflections from the pale sky. The air feels cold. Low-saturation steel-blue and gray-green tones dominate. The scene should have the emotional charge of ordinary northern European realism: a place of weekly routine, local history and small crowds, holding a subtle tension because something is about to begin here.
35mm Zeiss Super Speed Mk II, T4. Environmental wide. Readable depth across foreground terrace, pitch and opposite stand. Locked-off or barely breathing frame. WARDROBE
A heavily worn dark forest-green jacket, matte cotton or washed canvas, faded unevenly from years of use, slightly dirty around seams and collar, raised collar framing the neck.
Underneath: a visible off-white ribbed Feinripp tank top, slightly stretched, aged and imperfect, never bright white.
A washed-out dusty pink baseball cap, heavily faded and sun-bleached, soft worn cotton, slightly misshapen from years of use.

Narrow black wraparound sports sunglasses, late-1990s / early-2000s technical silhouette, close-fitting and slightly angular, but completely unbranded. No logos or writing on the temples or lenses. Matte, worn, faintly scratched rather than glossy.
Small simple metal hoop earrings in both ears, generic and unbranded.
Rough dark hair / grown-out mullet escaping naturally underneath the cap, slightly damp and wind-disordered.
A cigarette hangs loosely and asymmetrically from the corner of his mouth. Small amount of natural smoke. It should feel absent-minded rather than posed.
Nothing he wears should look newly purchased, styled, luxury, collectible or fashion-forward. Every object feels anonymous, personally owned and worn for years.
BACKGROUND
Photograph him against a simple neutral studio background, not at the campsite.
The background is a seamless, slightly textured muted gray / gray-green / cold concrete-toned studio backdrop, visually belonging to the same Baltic color universe as the film. No visible horizon line, no scenery, no furniture, no caravans, no architecture, no props.
It must still feel like ADAM / PATTERN rather than a clean photography studio: subdued, cold, slightly dirty tonality, restrained contrast, faint analog imperfection. Think of a character/casting portrait created inside the film world's visual grammar.
Do not use a pure white background, pure black background, warm beige fashion backdrop, colorful paper sweep or glossy commercial studio environment.
Lighting should emulate cold northern overcast daylight inside the studio: one large soft source from above/front-side, subtle negative fill on the opposite side, slightly underexposed face, deep but readable eye sockets. No beauty key, no rim light, no perfect symmetrical portrait illumination.
Frame him similarly to the second photographic reference: tight chest-up / head-and-shoulders portrait, slightly off-center, face occupying much of the frame, intimate camera distance.
85mm Zeiss Super Speed Mk II, T2.2. Near eye critically sharp. Gentle optical falloff across ears, hair and shoulders, but do not create extreme creamy bokeh.
The pink cap, black sunglasses, dark green jacket and off-white ribbed tank should create the only restrained color separation against the cold gray-green studio background.
The final image should feel as if this exact strange man was pulled into a tiny casting studio somewhere on the Baltic coast, stood in front of an ARRICAM LT for thirty seconds, smoked through the portrait and left again.
No posing. No cool-guy performance. No exaggerated vampire behavior. No visible fangs. No gothic codes. His vampiric quality comes only from the hollow fatigue, abnormal stillness and slightly unsettling permanence in his eyes.
ABSOLUTELY NO BRANDING: no Oakley logo, no sportswear logo, no cap logo, no letters, no symbols, no labels, no recognizable trademark shapes added intentionally, no text anywhere in the image.

SHOT 1 — INSIDE THE CAR / LEAVING THE STADIUM
Begin inside the moving car from the front passenger side, medium profile of Adam behind the wheel, 50mm, T2.4. He silently drives away from the Vereinshaus / football ground. Damp windshield, occasional windshield wiper crossing frame, gray dusk outside, distant yellow streetlights passing across his face. Adam looks tired and detached, eyes fixed on the road. No dialogue. No exaggerated acting. Camera has tiny natural vehicle vibration.
CUT ON THE WINDSHIELD WIPER.
SHOT 2 — LOW REAR THREE-QUARTER
Exterior road-level shot behind the station wagon as it pulls away from the stadium area and enters the edge of town. 35mm environmental composition. Wet asphalt reflects small warm pools of streetlight. The car accelerates gently away from camera. Bare trees and low provincial buildings frame the road.
CUT AS THE CAR PASSES BEHIND A FOREGROUND OBJECT.
SHOT 3 — SIDE STREET / SMALL EAST GERMAN TOWN
Static sidewalk-level composition looking down a quiet, almost deserted street lined with faded gray apartment buildings and old residential blocks. The car enters from one side, crosses the composition and continues toward the center of town. One distant cyclist or pedestrian may exist naturally in the background, but the town feels nearly empty. A few apartment windows glow warm against the gray evening.

MATCH CUT ON THE CAR'S FORWARD MOVEMENT.

Low 35mm tracking shot positioned slightly ahead and beside the car as it travels through the town. Camera moves briefly parallel to the station wagon while buildings slide past in deep perspective. Reflections from wet road and street lamps move organically across the bodywork.
Keep this shot short and tactile.
HARD CUT.
SHOT 5 — HIGH BIRD'S-EYE ABOVE THE TOWN
Suddenly jump in scale to a high near-vertical bird’s-eye view. The small gray station wagon is now only one moving element within the geometry of the quiet town. Long straight road, repetitive apartment blocks, sparse yellow streetlights, wet rooftops, almost no traffic.
Camera remains nearly static while Adam's car travels through the frame.
CUT WHEN THE CAR REACHES THE EDGE OF FRAME.
SHOT 6 — RURAL ROAD
Wide elevated 35mm-equivalent view of a narrow wet country road cutting through flat fields. Telephone poles, drainage ditches, patches of dead grass, isolated farmhouses and a dark tree line. Adam’s station wagon moves alone through the landscape.
No dramatic mountains, no picturesque sunset, no lush countryside. Flat, exposed, North German / Baltic terrain.
CUT ON FORWARD MOTION.
SHOT 7 — EXTREME TOP-DOWN COUNTRYSIDE
True vertical bird’s-eye shot from much higher altitude. The road creates a strong graphic line through muted brown-green fields. Adam's car is tiny but clearly moving along it.
The image should feel lonely and slightly absurd in scale — one small car traveling through a huge empty landscape.
Camera very slowly drifts forward with the car.
MATCH CUT ROAD LINE TO CAMPSITE ACCESS ROAD.
SHOT 8 — AERIAL REVEAL OF THE COASTAL CAMPSITE
High oblique bird’s-eye perspective revealing the modest campsite near the Baltic coast / tidal flats: rows of aging white caravans, old awnings, muddy grass, cracked concrete lanes, drainage canal, scattered older cars, plastic garden furniture, wind-battered flags and the cold gray water beyond the dike.
Adam's station wagon enters the campsite access road from the background.
The camera begins very high and slowly descends while following the car, creating the feeling that the entire journey is narrowing toward one specific tiny place.
No luxury campsite. No modern holiday resort. It should feel lived-in, slightly bleak and authentically provincial. This world is the grounded North German coastal setting of PATTERN.
SHOT 9 — FOLLOWING THROUGH THE CAMPSITE
Cut down to a lower rear three-quarter tracking angle, roughly waist height. The station wagon slowly drives between caravans on the cracked campsite lane. Foreground caravans and awnings pass close to camera, producing strong parallax. Small puddles, folding chairs, old camping equipment and wind moving loose fabric.
The car slows as Adam approaches his own pitch.
CUT AS A CARAVAN TEMPORARILY OCCLUDES THE CAR.
SHOT 10 — FINAL WIDE / ARRIVAL
Final locked-off elevated wide shot from approximately 4–6 meters above ground, looking slightly downward at Adam's campsite pitch.
The gray station wagon enters frame slowly, turns naturally into its familiar parking position beside his caravan / campsite setup and comes to a complete stop.
Brake lights glow softly for a moment.
The engine dies.
The windshield wipers make one final movement and stop.
Do not immediately show Adam getting out.
Hold the completely stationary car for the final beat while wind moves the grass and distant campsite objects.
After a sequence of constant movement, the final image becomes completely still.
END ON STILLNESS.

It should read clearly from above as the abandoned place Adam has just left behind. The composition is frontal and grounded, like a serious location still from a contemporary European drama.
SCENE STRUCTURE AND COMPOSITION:
The image is horizontally framed. In the left foreground stands a large, old white caravan cropped by the left image border so that only most of its side and rear are visible. Attached to it is a deep blue fabric awning / porch tent extending toward the center of the frame. In the right foreground stands another white caravan with a beige-brown awning attached, cropped by the right border. These two caravan setups frame the composition like two opposing camping plots, creating a corridor view into the campsite. Between them lies a muddy shared foreground area with worn grass, puddles, tire marks, and scattered trash.
WEATHER AND ATMOSPHERE:
The sky is fully clouded with thick, layered gray clouds, bright but sunless, with the flat, oppressive light of a damp North Sea day. The light is diffuse and shadow-poor. The ground is wet, trampled, and uneven. The overall mood is bleak, ordinary, provincial, and authentic, not romantic. It should feel like the morning after a cheap campsite gathering.
LEFT FOREGROUND CARAVAN:
The caravan on the left is an older European model, off-white to cream, with visible age and dirt. Its roof and the top of the awning are heavily weathered, stained, and mossy, with brown-green grime from years of exposure. The caravan side has horizontal trim stripes and old rectangular windows with slightly purple or dusty curtains visible inside. The attached awning is dark blue with transparent plastic window panels and beige piping. The blue awning looks old, practical, and slightly sagging, but still functional.
STRING LIGHTS:
Across the entrance edge of the left awning hangs a line of small round colored party bulbs. The bulbs are clearly visible and switched on despite the daylight. Use a mix of colors such as red, green, blue, yellow, and orange. They are casually strung, slightly uneven, and add a tiny note of shabby coziness.
LEFT FOREGROUND FURNITURE:
Directly in front of the left awning stands a white plastic camping table, slightly worn, rectangular or soft-edged rectangular, with a matte cheap plastic surface. Around it are three white plastic monobloc chairs: one in the near-left foreground facing slightly inward, one near the center tucked to the table, and one on the far side, partly inside the awning opening. On the table stand several beverage cans, arranged casually rather than neatly — around 3 to 4 cans, aluminum, mostly silver with printed labels. Inside the awning, another simple plastic chair is visible in shadow. The interior of the awning contains a few modest camping objects, but remains mostly dark.
CENTER FOREGROUND OBJECT:
In the immediate foreground center stands a black kettle-style charcoal grill with a rounded lid and metal tripod legs. It is weathered, used, and realistic, not brand-new. The grill is placed directly on muddy grass. A thin electric cable or extension cord lies loosely on the wet ground nearby, snaking across the foreground.
RIGHT FOREGROUND SETUP:
To the right of center is a cheap black plastic table with a matte surface. On top of it stands a row of multiple drink cans, perhaps 6 to 8, casually grouped. Beside and behind this table are two dark plastic garden chairs, slightly worn, simple stackable style, facing loosely toward the middle of the image. The right caravan’s attached awning is beige and brown with cloudy plastic windows, also visibly weathered and inexpensive.

Between the two foreground camping plots, slightly right of center, sits a small inflatable kiddie pool made of bright medium blue plastic. It is shallow and round. Inside the pool are many empty aluminum drink cans floating or lying in the bottom, making it look absurd, trashy, and very campsite-real. The pool is one of the key visual details and should be clearly readable.
GROUND DETAIL:
The entire foreground and midground ground surface is muddy, patchy, and heavily used. Grass grows in irregular tufts among bare mud. There are puddles, wheel ruts, and compacted wet soil. Scattered across the ground — especially in the right foreground and around the pool — are numerous empty crushed and uncrushed drink cans. The litter should feel believable and specific, not excessive to the point of looking like a garbage dump. The terrain must look authentically wet and cold.

[SHOT] A very high, almost perfectly vertical bird’s-eye view looking straight down onto the Baltic Sea dike road. Environmental wide shot, 35mm, T4. The composition must feel extremely deliberate, graphic and symmetrical while remaining completely photorealistic and geographically believable.
ABSOLUTE SCREEN-POSITION AND MOVEMENT LOCK
ADAM MUST BE IN THE LOWER HALF OF THE IMAGE.
Adam is positioned below the bench and below the visual midpoint, on the central asphalt road. He is walking DOWNWARD toward the BOTTOM EDGE of the frame, moving farther and farther away from the bench.
His walking direction is unmistakably toward the bottom of the image. His body orientation, stride and shoulders must clearly communicate that he is moving downward. He does not walk toward the woman, does not walk upward, and does not turn around.
THE ELDERLY WOMAN MUST BE IN THE UPPER HALF OF THE IMAGE.
The elderly woman on the bicycle is positioned above the bench and noticeably farther toward the TOP of the frame than Adam is toward the bottom. She is already slightly farther away from the central meeting point.
She rides UPWARD toward the TOP EDGE of the frame, continuing away from the bench and away from Adam. Her bicycle orientation must unmistakably point toward the top of the image.
They are travelling in exactly opposite directions and actively increasing the distance between them:
GRANDMOTHER → TOP OF FRAME
ADAM → BOTTOM OF FRAME
They must NEVER appear to approach one another.
The narrow asphalt dike road runs vertically through the exact middle of the frame from the bottom edge toward the top edge, forming the central visual axis. The camera is positioned directly above the road.
Exactly between the two characters is the empty weathered wooden bench from the previous scene. The bench acts as the emotional and compositional point from which they have separated.
The spatial order from TOP to BOTTOM must be unmistakably:
TOP EDGE
elderly woman riding bicycle upward and away
large stretch of empty road
empty wooden bench near the midpoint
stretch of empty road
Adam walking downward and away
BOTTOM EDGE
Adam is recognizable from above by his washed faded pink bucket hat, dark green-black worn jacket, black trousers and slim silhouette. His posture is relaxed and slightly tired. He walks alone toward the bottom edge and never looks back.
The elderly German camping woman is recognizable from above by her dusty rose-pink cardigan, patterned headscarf, beige trousers and traditional dark bicycle. She rides slowly toward the top edge. She should sit noticeably higher in the frame, already further along her journey away from Adam.
Both characters remain relatively small within the landscape. There must be a significant amount of empty asphalt between Adam, the bench and the woman, emphasizing that the encounter has ended.
The bench is modest, slightly worn, practical North German coastal infrastructure rather than a picturesque park bench. It stands immediately beside the asphalt on the narrow grass shoulder of the dike. No person is sitting on it.
The image is divided into three strong longitudinal landscape zones.
RIGHT SIDE: the Baltic Sea fills almost the entire right side of the frame. Cold gray-blue water, small irregular wind-driven ripples, subtle parallel lines of waves close to shore. No boats, no dramatic surf, no tropical blue water. The coastline runs approximately parallel to the road.
CENTER: the raised grassy dike with the narrow asphalt road along its crest. Wind-flattened yellow-green and gray-green coastal grass surrounds the road. The road is old but maintained, slightly faded and imperfect, without road markings. The central dike creates a clean geographic separation between land and sea.
LEFT SIDE: broad flat North German grassland and marshland stretching away from the dike, muted olive-green and brown-green vegetation, drainage channels and subtle irregular patches of coastal meadow. No buildings dominating the frame, no dramatic cliffs, no mountains, no trees forming a forest.
The overall composition should remain highly controlled and nearly diagrammatic: sea on the right, grassland on the left, the dike road as the central spine.
However, do not mirror the two characters into identical positions. The elderly cyclist should already be slightly farther away and higher toward the top edge, while Adam remains somewhat closer to the central bench in the lower half.
Keep large areas of negative space around both characters. Do not crowd the frame with objects.
No other pedestrians, cyclists, cars, signs or tourists.
The camera is completely static and distant, observing the separation rather than following either character. Genuine high-altitude photographic perspective, not a synthetic satellite image or exaggerated drone look. Straight natural geometry, minimal wide-angle distortion, realistic human proportions.
Soft northern European daylight under broken coastal cloud cover. The land and water retain enough brightness and detail to remain readable; do not make the image excessively dark or stormy. Cool steel-blue sea, gray-green grass and asphalt, with Adam’s faded pink hat and the woman’s muted dusty-pink cardigan providing the only restrained warmer color accents.
The emotional idea is separation and stillness: two people who briefly crossed paths are now moving in opposite directions away from the same abandoned bench.
CRITICAL COMPOSITION RULE: Adam = lower part of image, walking toward bottom edge. Elderly woman = upper part of image, riding toward top edge. They are moving AWAY FROM EACH OTHER, never toward each other.

The town feels strangely quiet and slightly dead, but NOT abandoned.
Wide empty sidewalks, damp asphalt, patched road surfaces, faded lane markings, cracked curbs and almost no traffic. The street appears designed for a town that once had more people in it.
Architecture should strongly but naturally suggest provincial eastern Germany: faded two- and three-storey stucco buildings, modest pre-war houses, simple GDR-era residential architecture, occasional low Plattenbau blocks in the distance, concrete bus shelters, rows of old garages, aging balconies, satellite dishes, utility boxes and small post-socialist commercial buildings.
Ground-floor storefronts are mostly dark and closed. Large empty shop windows, shutters or curtains, but absolutely NO readable signs, logos, advertisements or text.
Only very sparse signs of life: one elderly cyclist in the distance, perhaps a lone person waiting at a bus stop, one dog walker far down a side street, a few warm apartment windows glowing above otherwise dark façades. No crowds.
Pass an almost empty small-town market square or intersection with oversized paved space, a few empty benches, aging street trees, old metal railings and a nearly empty parking area.
The town should feel inhabited but dormant — as if everything closed at 6 PM and by dusk almost everyone has disappeared indoors.
Camera movement is restrained and observational. Natural forward travel with subtle lateral parallax as buildings, lampposts and parked cars drift past the frame. No dramatic acceleration, no gimbal perfection, no commercial driving-shot aesthetic.
35mm lens, T4, deep readable environmental detail. Keep foreground façades, midground street architecture and distant residential blocks all spatially legible. Slight natural motion softness only in the closest passing objects while the deeper town remains readable.
The emotional target is quiet provincial emptiness: former East German small-town stillness at dusk, damp and faded, neither picturesque nor dramatically derelict. A transitional moment where the noise of the football match has vanished and the world suddenly feels almost completely still.

The occupied plots are closer together than in a sparse campsite, but still clearly separated and individually understandable. The density should feel natural, not chaotic.
The caravans are mostly old, modest white or beige European caravans from the 1980s, 1990s and early 2000s. Some have attached awnings or simple porch tents in muted blue-gray fabric. The campsite should not contain shiny luxury motorhomes or modern designer campers.

The cars should look slightly worn-in, practical, and normal: older Volkswagen, Opel, Ford, Renault, Skoda-type energy, with muted paint colors such as dark blue, faded silver, dull green, gray, burgundy, or black. They should fit the world of budget camping.
In the foreground, place a caravan with an attached blue-gray awning. In front of this caravan, clearly visible and important in the composition, there is a white plastic camping table and several white plastic chairs arranged casually on the grass. Small warm string lights are attached around the awning entrance or edge, glowing subtly and giving a tiny note of human coziness against the bleak weather. This foreground setup should feel very believable and lived in, not staged too perfectly.
Across the campsite, distribute camping-typical objects in a restrained, well-dosed way. The key is realism through selective detail, not clutter. On some plots there may be a charcoal grill, on another a folding chair, on another a drying rack, a small cooler box, a bicycle, a plastic crate, a simple windbreak, or a modest camping table. On one plot, include a small inflated blue plastic kiddie pool, placed casually in the little “garden” area of the pitch. These accessories should feel unevenly distributed and individualized, as if each camper has brought a few personal objects, but no plot should look overloaded or theatrical. Avoid over-decoration.

Above the entrance, the sign must clearly read exactly: “Rezeption” with a Z. The lettering should feel plain and utilitarian, as on a real cheap German campsite, not like a polished graphic design. In front of the building are a few white plastic chairs and a small table on a simple wooden or concrete area. The building feels functional, a bit tired, but still in use.
The ground throughout the campsite is damp and uneven, with muddy tire tracks, puddles, worn grass, and rutted edges along the road. The central lane is cracked concrete with patches and water-filled depressions. The drainage ditch on the right contains dark water and reinforces the flat, wind-beaten coastal landscape. Flags on poles may appear here and there, fluttering lightly in the wind.
The overall mood should be melancholic, mundane and highly believable: a bleak North German camping holiday atmosphere, cheap but affectionate, ordinary but cinematically rich. The image should feel like a real location photograph from a serious contemporary European film, not an AI fantasy image. They are travelling in exactly opposite directions and actively increasing the distance between them:
GRANDMOTHER → TOP OF FRAME
ADAM → BOTTOM OF FRAME
They must NEVER appear to approach one another.
The narrow asphalt dike road runs vertically through the exact middle of the frame from the bottom edge toward the top edge, forming the central visual axis. The camera is positioned directly above the road.

The spatial order from TOP to BOTTOM must be unmistakably:
TOP EDGE
elderly woman riding bicycle upward and away
large stretch of empty road
empty wooden bench near the midpoint
stretch of empty road
Adam walking downward and away
BOTTOM EDGE
Adam is recognizable from above by his washed faded pink bucket hat, dark green-black worn jacket, black trousers and slim silhouette. His posture is relaxed and slightly tired. He walks alone toward the bottom edge and never looks back.
The elderly German camping woman is recognizable from above by her dusty rose-pink cardigan, patterned headscarf, beige trousers and traditional dark bicycle. She rides slowly toward the top edge. She should sit noticeably higher in the frame, already further along her journey away from Adam.
Both characters remain relatively small within the landscape. There must be a significant amount of empty asphalt between Adam, the bench and the woman, emphasizing that the encounter has ended.
The bench is modest, slightly worn, practical North German coastal infrastructure rather than a picturesque park bench. It stands immediately beside the asphalt on the narrow grass shoulder of the dike. No person is sitting on it.
The image is divided into three strong longitudinal landscape zones.
RIGHT SIDE: the Baltic Sea fills almost the entire right side of the frame. Cold gray-blue water, small irregular wind-driven ripples, subtle parallel lines of waves close to shore. No boats, no dramatic surf, no tropical blue water. The coastline runs approximately parallel to the road.
CENTER: the raised grassy dike with the narrow asphalt road along its crest. Wind-flattened yellow-green and gray-green coastal grass surrounds the road. The road is old but maintained, slightly faded and imperfect, without road markings. The central dike creates a clean geographic separation between land and sea.
LEFT SIDE: broad flat North German grassland and marshland stretching away from the dike, muted olive-green and brown-green vegetation, drainage channels and subtle irregular patches of coastal meadow. No buildings dominating the frame, no dramatic cliffs, no mountains, no trees forming a forest.
The overall composition should remain highly controlled and nearly diagrammatic: sea on the right, grassland on the left, the dike road as the central spine.
However, do not mirror the two characters into identical positions. The elderly cyclist should already be slightly farther away and higher toward the top edge, while Adam remains somewhat closer to the central bench in the lower half.
Keep large areas of negative space around both characters. Do not crowd the frame with objects.
No other pedestrians, cyclists, cars, signs or tourists.
The camera is completely static and distant, observing the separation rather than following either character. Genuine high-altitude photographic perspective, not a synthetic satellite image or exaggerated drone look. Straight natural geometry, minimal wide-angle distortion, realistic human proportions.
Soft northern European daylight under broken coastal cloud cover. The land and water retain enough brightness and detail to remain readable; do not make the image excessively dark or stormy. Cool steel-blue sea, gray-green grass and asphalt, with Adam’s faded pink hat and the woman’s muted dusty-pink cardigan providing the only restrained warmer color accents.
The emotional idea is separation and stillness: two people who briefly crossed paths are now moving in opposite directions away from the same abandoned bench.
CRITICAL COMPOSITION RULE: Adam = lower part of image, walking toward bottom edge. Elderly woman = upper part of image, riding toward top edge. They are moving AWAY FROM EACH OTHER, never toward each other.

[SHOT] Environmental wide of a quiet rural road outside the small East German town, continuing the journey toward the campsite at dusk.
The town has disappeared behind us. A narrow two-lane Landstraße cuts through flat, sparse countryside in the Baltic hinterland. The road feels distinctly provincial and East German rather than picturesque: slightly patched damp asphalt, faded white edge markings, narrow shoulders, shallow drainage ditches and occasional old reflector posts.
No car is visible anywhere in the frame. No hood, windshield, dashboard, mirrors or vehicle reflections. Adam is not visible. The image should simply establish the lonely stretch of road connecting the town to the campsite.
The road runs diagonally or gently curves through the landscape, disappearing between distant rows of dark trees. On either side are subdued agricultural fields, slightly overgrown roadside grass, patches of brown soil, thin birch trees, old windbreaks, occasional concrete utility poles and sparse wooden fences.
A few distant traces of habitation remain: an isolated farmhouse, an old agricultural shed, a tiny cluster of modest houses or a weathered bus shelter far beside the road. Everything is widely spaced and almost completely still.
It is noticeably later now. Dusk is settling in. The pale lavender-gray and pearl-gray sky still retains enough ambient light to clearly read the landscape, but the ground is beginning to darken. No dramatic sunset and no visible sun.
There should be a subtle progression toward greater isolation: the road begins relatively open between fields and gradually leads toward a darker belt of pines and mixed woodland in the distance, suggesting that the campsite lies somewhere beyond.
Absolutely no visible sea, beach, dunes or tourist infrastructure. This is inland rural Mecklenburg-Vorpommern / former East German coastal hinterland atmosphere — flat, quiet, slightly forgotten and functional.
No dramatic mountains, no beautiful sweeping countryside, no idyllic golden fields. The landscape should feel ordinary enough to be slightly unsettling.
Composition should strongly emphasize the empty road as the visual spine of the frame. Plenty of negative space. Very little human activity. Perhaps one distant weak streetlamp or a single warm farmhouse window beginning to glow, but otherwise almost no artificial light.
35mm lens, T4, deep readable environmental background. Camera positioned slightly elevated from the roadside, not aerial, with the road receding naturally into the distance. Locked-off observational frame or extremely subtle handheld breathing drift.
The emotional target is the feeling of leaving the last traces of town behind: the world becoming quieter, darker and emptier with every kilometer, moving toward the isolated campsite.

[SHOT] Moving environmental POV during early dusk, traveling from the local football stadium toward the campsite through a small, almost lifeless East German town.
IMPORTANT COMPOSITION RULE: THE CAR ITSELF IS NEVER VISIBLE. No hood, no dashboard, no windshield frame, no rear-view mirror, no side mirror, no door frame, no reflections revealing the vehicle. The camera simply moves through the town at the natural speed and height of a slowly driven car, creating the feeling of watching the town pass from inside a vehicle without ever showing the vehicle itself.
The camera travels steadily along a slightly oversized provincial main street through a modest former-GDR Kleinstadt near the Baltic region, but clearly inland. Absolutely no sea, beach or coastal promenade visible.
It is already dusk. The last daylight is fading into a pale pearl-gray and dusty lavender-gray sky. Streetlights have just started coming on, creating isolated weak pools of nicotine-yellow sodium light against the cool evening.
The town feels strangely quiet and slightly dead, but NOT abandoned.
Wide empty sidewalks, damp asphalt, patched road surfaces, faded lane markings, cracked curbs and almost no traffic. The street appears designed for a town that once had more people in it.
Architecture should strongly but naturally suggest provincial eastern Germany: faded two- and three-storey stucco buildings, modest pre-war houses, simple GDR-era residential architecture, occasional low Plattenbau blocks in the distance, concrete bus shelters, rows of old garages, aging balconies, satellite dishes, utility boxes and small post-socialist commercial buildings.
Ground-floor storefronts are mostly dark and closed. Large empty shop windows, shutters or curtains, but absolutely NO readable signs, logos, advertisements or text.
Only very sparse signs of life: one elderly cyclist in the distance, perhaps a lone person waiting at a bus stop, one dog walker far down a side street, a few warm apartment windows glowing above otherwise dark façades. No crowds.
Pass an almost empty small-town market square or intersection with oversized paved space, a few empty benches, aging street trees, old metal railings and a nearly empty parking area.
The town should feel inhabited but dormant — as if everything closed at 6 PM and by dusk almost everyone has disappeared indoors.
Camera movement is restrained and observational. Natural forward travel with subtle lateral parallax as buildings, lampposts and parked cars drift past the frame. No dramatic acceleration, no gimbal perfection, no commercial driving-shot aesthetic.
35mm lens, T4, deep readable environmental detail. Keep foreground façades, midground street architecture and distant residential blocks all spatially legible. Slight natural motion softness only in the closest passing objects while the deeper town remains readable.
The emotional target is quiet provincial emptiness: former East German small-town stillness at dusk, damp and faded, neither picturesque nor dramatically derelict. A transitional moment where the noise of the football match has vanished and the world suddenly feels almost completely still.

Adam wears his characteristic HAT exactly as established in the reference images for the ENTIRE sequence. HE NEVER REMOVES IT.
Adam ALWAYS wears his small, subtle GOLD CHAIN around his neck.
Adam has ABSOLUTELY NO HAND TATTOOS and NO FINGER TATTOOS.
NO RINGS.
NO BRACELETS.
Adam wears his established dark leather LOAFERS.
Adam is SMOKING THROUGHOUT THE ENTIRE SEQUENCE. The cigarette remains lit and physically consistent from beginning to end. It may rest naturally in the corner of his mouth or between his fingers.
Adam also carries a pair of simple BLACK LEATHER GLOVES and PUTS THEM ON WHILE WALKING THROUGH THE VEREINSGASTSTÄTTE.
The gloves are plain black leather, slightly worn, soft and fitted, with subtle natural creasing.
NO logos.
NO metal studs.
NO tactical appearance.
NO biker styling.
NO decorative stitching.
They should look like understated old black leather driving gloves without visible branding.
OPENING:
The camera begins inside the old German Vereinsgaststätte facing toward the football-side entrance.
Adam enters from the rainy amateur football ground.
For the first moment Adam is in the foreground while DIRECTLY BEHIND HIM through the open doorway the small football world remains clearly visible in VERY DEEP FOCUS:
the wet football pitch,
players actively playing,
the referee,
the tiny opposite spectator stand,
local spectators,
simple floodlight poles,
rain,
and the flat Baltic coastal landscape.
Do NOT blur the football field into bokeh.
The match is fully alive behind him while Adam remains completely detached.
We clearly hear:
rain,
boots hitting wet grass,
indistinct player shouts,
spectators reacting,
an occasional referee whistle.
NO understandable dialogue.
NO announcer.
NO MUSIC.
Adam simply walks inside while smoking.
INSIDE THE VEREINSGASTSTÄTTE:
The room is large, dark, woody, muffig and authentically northern German.
Dark wooden wall paneling.
Heavy beams.
Old wooden tables and chairs.
Long dark bar.
Old tiled floor.
Weak nicotine-yellow lamps.
Cold fluorescent contamination.
A few old fictional football Wimpel.
Only a few small amateur trophies.
Dartboards.
Old team photographs.
Temporary blue-and-white Oktoberfest garlands hang loosely between the beams.
A removable decorative wall element displays only:
“OKTOBERFEST”
The decoration feels temporary and locally improvised, not like a permanent Bavarian theme bar.
LOAFER DETAIL:
As Adam continues walking, the camera naturally DIPS DOWN without cutting.
For roughly 1–2 seconds we clearly see his worn DARK LEATHER LOAFERS crossing the old tiled floor.
Slightly damp soles.
Scratched beige-gray-brown tiles.
Old grout.
Small stains.
Subtle moisture.
Natural hard footsteps.
No slow motion.
No fashion framing.
The camera rises again while Adam continues moving.
BLACK LEATHER GLOVES:
While continuing to walk through the Vereinsgaststätte, Adam CASUALLY PUTS ON HIS BLACK LEATHER GLOVES.
This happens naturally within his movement and must NOT stop his walk.
He places the cigarette loosely in the corner of his mouth so BOTH HANDS are available.
Before the gloves cover them, his bare hands are briefly visible and clearly have:
NO HAND TATTOOS.
NO FINGER TATTOOS.
NO RINGS.
He first slides one hand into the first black leather glove.
Using the already-gloved hand, he casually pulls the second glove over the other hand.
He gives each glove one small natural tug at the wrist to seat it properly.
The action is practiced, effortless and habitual.
No dramatic close-up.
No assassin cliché.
No threatening gesture.
No exaggerated leather sounds.
He simply puts them on while walking, as though preparing to go back outside into the cold rain.
The cigarette remains naturally held in his mouth during the action and NEVER disappears.
Once both gloves are on, ADAM KEEPS THE BLACK LEATHER GLOVES ON FOR THE REST OF THE SEQUENCE.
He wears them:
while passing the Gastwirt,
through the corridor,
when opening the rear door,
across the parking lot,
when opening the car,
while getting into the driver's seat,
and when driving away.
GASTWIRT:
At the wooden counter stands the run-down Gastwirt.
Late 50s / early 60s.
Thin tired face.
Gray stubble.
Receding greasy hair.
Heavy bags under his eyes.
Faded work shirt.
As Adam passes, the Gastwirt briefly looks up.
Adam, now wearing the black leather gloves, and the Gastwirt exchange ONE TINY FAMILIAR NOD.
No smile.
No words.
No handshake.
No stopping.
The Gastwirt immediately goes back to what he was doing.
SOUND INSIDE:
As the entrance door closes behind Adam, the football game becomes noticeably MUFFLED.
We can still hear:
faint spectators,
occasional referee whistles,
distant player shouts.
Inside we hear:
Adam’s loafers on tile,
quiet fluorescent hum,
subtle glass sounds,
small room creaks,
his cigarette inhale and exhale,
very subtle natural leather movement while he pulls on the gloves.
NO MUSIC.
NO SCORE.
NO VOICE-OVER.
CORRIDOR AND EXIT:
Adam continues into the narrow back corridor.
The camera naturally moves from in front of him to slightly behind and beside him.
No impossible camera movement.
He reaches the rear door and opens it with his BLACK LEATHER GLOVED HAND.
Cold rainy daylight enters.
The camera follows him onto the parking lot IN THE SAME TAKE.
Once the Vereinsheim is physically between Adam and the football pitch, the game rapidly becomes distant and almost inaudible.
The dominant sounds are now:
rain on asphalt,
soft coastal wind,
Adam’s footsteps,
small puddle splashes.
The parking lot feels noticeably quiet and isolated.
PARKING LOT:
Adam walks toward his old black convertible.
Behind him sits the Vereinsheim.
Parts of the tiny amateur stadium remain visible around the building:
a floodlight pole,
part of the wet pitch,
a section of the tiny covered stand.
The actual match now feels far away.
Adam keeps smoking.
Hat stays on.
Gold chain stays on.
Black leather gloves stay on.
THE CAR:
Adam’s car is the established fictional late-1970s / early-1980s European compact convertible.
Distinctly NOT a VW Golf Cabriolet.
Slightly longer low hood.
Lower beltline.
Narrower body.
Flat squared front.
Two widely spaced round headlights.
Narrow plain grille.
Thin dark bumpers.
Black aged paint.
Closed dark fabric soft top.
Simple chrome mirrors.
Old silver mesh-style wheels.
Muted tobacco-brown interior.
NO manufacturer badge.
NO grille emblem.
NO hood emblem.
NO model lettering.
NO wheel logos.
It has an old German pre-EU license plate:
white plate,
black characters,
thin black border,
slightly weathered,
NO blue EU stripe.
GETTING IN AND DRIVING AWAY:
Adam approaches the DRIVER’S SIDE.
Still smoking.
Still wearing his hat.
Still wearing the gold chain.
Still wearing BOTH BLACK LEATHER GLOVES.
He reaches for the driver's door with one gloved hand and opens it.
The dark leather glove should be clearly visible against the old wet car door.
No dramatic gesture.
No car-commercial moment.
He bends down and naturally gets into the driver's seat.
The camera remains OUTSIDE.
We briefly glimpse the muted old interior.
Adam closes the door.
He starts the old car.
The engine turns over with a slightly rough but believable mechanical sound.
No aggressive revving.
The windshield is covered with rain droplets.
The old windshield wipers make one slow sweep.
Adam remains smoking inside the car.
He puts the car into gear and calmly PULLS AWAY.
No burnout.
No wheelspin.
No aggressive acceleration.
The black convertible slowly rolls across the wet parking lot and onto the small road.
The camera stays behind.
The car becomes smaller in frame.
Rain continues falling.
The old engine sound slowly disappears into the quiet Baltic environment.
END with Adam driving away, leaving the Vereinsheim and tiny football ground behind.
CRITICAL RULES:
ONE CONTINUOUS 15-SECOND TAKE.
NO CUTS.
NO MONTAGE.
NO TELEPORTATION.
NO SPEED RAMPS.
NO SLOW MOTION.
NO MUSIC.
NO SCORE.
NO VOICE-OVER.
FOOTBALL LOUD AND CLEAR AT THE BEGINNING.
MUFFLED INSIDE THE VEREINSHEIM.
ALMOST COMPLETELY GONE ON THE PARKING LOT.
ADAM WEARS HIS HAT THE ENTIRE TIME.
ADAM ALWAYS WEARS HIS SMALL GOLD CHAIN.
ADAM SMOKES THROUGHOUT THE ENTIRE SEQUENCE.
THE CIGARETTE NEVER DISAPPEARS.
ADAM'S BARE HANDS HAVE NO TATTOOS AND NO RINGS.
WHILE WALKING THROUGH THE VEREINSGASTSTÄTTE, HE PUTS ON TWO PLAIN BLACK LEATHER GLOVES.
THE CIGARETTE RESTS IN HIS MOUTH WHILE HE PUTS THEM ON.
AFTERWARD, THE BLACK LEATHER GLOVES STAY ON UNTIL THE END.
CLEAR BRIEF VIEW OF HIS DARK LOAFERS WALKING OVER THE OLD TILES.
ADAM GETS INTO THE DRIVER'S SIDE.
HE STARTS THE CAR.
HE DRIVES AWAY THROUGH THE RAIN.

Default to a 50mm lens at T2.0-T2.8; use 35mm only for environmental wides and 85mm only for close-ups. Strong optical depth separation with the subject sharply resolved and the background soft but still recognizable - never artificial bokeh. Natural overcast skylight, negative fill, motivated tungsten practicals at night, no beauty lighting. Muted Baltic palette: steel-blue and gray-green atmosphere, restrained warm skin, nicotine-yellow practicals, soft highlight roll-off, slightly lifted blacks, low saturation. Medium-fine authentic 35mm grain, subtle halation, tiny organic imperfections, no HDR, no digital crispness, no glossy commercial finish. Skin must remain real: pores, under-eye texture, stubble, moisture, small imperfections. Camera is intimate and observational, eye-level or slightly low, controlled handheld micro-drift or locked-off frames, never smooth gimbal movement. The world feels damp, wind-worn, lived-in and slightly faded. Preserve this exact visual grammar in every shot.
NEGATIVE LOCK: No glossy advertising light, no fashion pose, no hyper-clean AI skin, no HDR micro-contrast, no oversaturated color, no teal-orange grade, no extreme anamorphic flares, no excessive fog, no heavy 16mm grain, no surreal lens distortion, no shallow-focus blur that erases the environment, no new camera or lens system.
[SHOT] A very high, almost perfectly vertical bird’s-eye view looking straight down onto the Baltic Sea dike road. Environmental wide shot, 35mm, T4. The composition must feel extremely deliberate, graphic and symmetrical while remaining completely photorealistic and geographically believable.
ABSOLUTE SCREEN-POSITION AND MOVEMENT LOCK
ADAM MUST BE IN THE LOWER HALF OF THE IMAGE.
Adam is positioned below the bench and below the visual midpoint, on the central asphalt road. He is walking DOWNWARD toward the BOTTOM EDGE of the frame, moving farther and farther away from the bench.
His walking direction is unmistakably toward the bottom of the image. His body orientation, stride and shoulders must clearly communicate that he is moving downward. He does not walk toward the woman, does not walk upward, and does not turn around.
THE ELDERLY WOMAN MUST BE IN THE UPPER HALF OF THE IMAGE.
The elderly woman on the bicycle is positioned above the bench and noticeably farther toward the TOP of the frame than Adam is toward the bottom. She is already slightly farther away from the central meeting point.
She rides UPWARD toward the TOP EDGE of the frame, continuing away from the bench and away from Adam. Her bicycle orientation must unmistakably point toward the top of the image.
They are travelling in exactly opposite directions and actively increasing the distance between them:
GRANDMOTHER → TOP OF FRAME
ADAM → BOTTOM OF FRAME
They must NEVER appear to approach one another.
The narrow asphalt dike road runs vertically through the exact middle of the frame from the bottom edge toward the top edge, forming the central visual axis. The camera is positioned directly above the road.
Exactly between the two characters is the empty weathered wooden bench from the previous scene. The bench acts as the emotional and compositional point from which they have separated.
The spatial order from TOP to BOTTOM must be unmistakably:
TOP EDGE
elderly woman riding bicycle upward and away
large stretch of empty road
empty wooden bench near the midpoint
stretch of empty road
Adam walking downward and away
BOTTOM EDGE
Adam is recognizable from above by his washed faded pink bucket hat, dark green-black worn jacket, black trousers and slim silhouette. His posture is relaxed and slightly tired. He walks alone toward the bottom edge and never looks back.
The elderly German camping woman is recognizable from above by her dusty rose-pink cardigan, patterned headscarf, beige trousers and traditional dark bicycle. She rides slowly toward the top edge. She should sit noticeably higher in the frame, already further along her journey away from Adam.
Both characters remain relatively small within the landscape. There must be a significant amount of empty asphalt between Adam, the bench and the woman, emphasizing that the encounter has ended.
The bench is modest, slightly worn, practical North German coastal infrastructure rather than a picturesque park bench. It stands immediately beside the asphalt on the narrow grass shoulder of the dike. No person is sitting on it.
The image is divided into three strong longitudinal landscape zones.
RIGHT SIDE: the Baltic Sea fills almost the entire right side of the frame. Cold gray-blue water, small irregular wind-driven ripples, subtle parallel lines of waves close to shore. No boats, no dramatic surf, no tropical blue water. The coastline runs approximately parallel to the road.
CENTER: the raised grassy dike with the narrow asphalt road along its crest. Wind-flattened yellow-green and gray-green coastal grass surrounds the road. The road is old but maintained, slightly faded and imperfect, without road markings. The central dike creates a clean geographic separation between land and sea.
LEFT SIDE: broad flat North German grassland and marshland stretching away from the dike, muted olive-green and brown-green vegetation, drainage channels and subtle irregular patches of coastal meadow. No buildings dominating the frame, no dramatic cliffs, no mountains, no trees forming a forest.
The overall composition should remain highly controlled and nearly diagrammatic: sea on the right, grassland on the left, the dike road as the central spine.
However, do not mirror the two characters into identical positions. The elderly cyclist should already be slightly farther away and higher toward the top edge, while Adam remains somewhat closer to the central bench in the lower half.
Keep large areas of negative space around both characters. Do not crowd the frame with objects.
No other pedestrians, cyclists, cars, signs or tourists.
The camera is completely static and distant, observing the separation rather than following either character. Genuine high-altitude photographic perspective, not a synthetic satellite image or exaggerated drone look. Straight natural geometry, minimal wide-angle distortion, realistic human proportions.
Soft northern European daylight under broken coastal cloud cover. The land and water retain enough brightness and detail to remain readable; do not make the image excessively dark or stormy. Cool steel-blue sea, gray-green grass and asphalt, with Adam’s faded pink hat and the woman’s muted dusty-pink cardigan providing the only restrained warmer color accents.
The emotional idea is separation and stillness: two people who briefly crossed paths are now moving in opposite directions away from the same abandoned bench.
CRITICAL COMPOSITION RULE: Adam = lower part of image, walking toward bottom edge. Elderly woman = upper part of image, riding toward top edge. They are moving AWAY FROM EACH OTHER, never toward each other.

The old folding bike makes quiet squeaking and creaking sounds, with a faint rattling chain and small metallic noises as she passes.
Natural sound only: soft coastal wind, occasional stronger whistling gusts, distant unseen sea surf, irregular seagulls, subtle old-bicycle squeaks. No dialogue, no music.
Photorealistic real-time motion, restrained European cinema, realistic wind physics, subtle 35mm film texture.

Authentic medium-fine 35mm grain, subtle halation, soft highlight roll-off, slightly lifted blacks, low saturation, no HDR, no digital crispness, no glossy commercial finish.

Muted Baltic night palette:
deep steel-blue and gray-green darkness,
dirty nicotine-yellow caravan practicals,
restrained skin tones.

REFERENCE LOCK:

@img1 and @img2 = ADAM.
Use only for Adam’s exact face, hair, facial structure, neck tattoos and styling.
Adam is the younger man.
His wraparound sunglasses MUST remain visibly resting on top of his head.
No tattoos on Adam’s hands, fingers or arms.

@img3, @img4, @img5 and @img6 = SICKO.
Use only for Sicko’s exact facial identity, age, thin build, hollow cheeks, very large gray-green eyes, receding thin hair, clothing and tattoo details.
@img6 defines Sicko’s hand tattoos.

@img7 = CAMPSITE ENVIRONMENT REFERENCE ONLY.
Use it only for the visual character of the campsite:
modest caravans,
weathered surfaces,
narrow camping lanes,
small plots,
warm windows,
damp Baltic atmosphere.
Do NOT copy the aerial composition.

SHOT:

Night on the campsite.

Adam and Sicko walk casually side by side through the campsite while talking to each other.

The camera is VERY close to them, approximately 50–70 cm away.

This is a tight shared two-person close-up.
Their faces and heads dominate the frame.
Only a little neck and upper shoulder area is visible.

CAMERA ANGLE — IMPORTANT:

The camera is NOT directly centered in front of them.

Instead, it moves slightly diagonally ahead of them, offset to one side of their walking path.

The camera travels backward at a subtle diagonal while Adam and Sicko continue walking forward.

Because of this angle, they are not walking straight into the lens.
They move slightly across the frame and gradually PASS BY the camera.

The perspective should feel like the camera briefly intercepts their walk before they naturally continue past it.

Neither man ever looks into the camera.

Their attention stays on each other or naturally forward along the campsite path.

This should feel observational and accidental, not like actors performing toward a camera.

COMPOSITION:

Both faces remain simultaneously sharp.

One man may sit fractionally closer to camera than the other, creating subtle depth and asymmetry, but neither face may become soft.

Do not perfectly center them.
Do not make the composition symmetrical.

The frame should feel alive and naturally imperfect.

They are walking close enough together that both faces remain the visual focus.

Their mouths are completely still in this exact frozen moment.
No visible talking.
No open mouths.
This is an instant between spoken lines.

Adam feels restrained, dry, slightly amused.
Sicko feels relaxed, attentive and engaged.

ENVIRONMENT:

Only the campsite is visible in the background.

NO sea.
NO beach.
NO dike.
NO coastline.
NO horizon.
NO landscape beyond the campsite.

Behind them are only:
caravans,
small camping plots,
warm illuminated caravan windows,
awnings,
plastic chairs,
small fences,
camping tables,
patches of grass,
gravel or worn asphalt,
occasional modest campsite lamps.

The campsite should feel slightly old, damp, wind-worn and lived-in.

Warm windows recede deeply behind them and create small points of life inside the dark campsite.

LIGHTING — CRITICAL:

There is NO direct light on their faces.

No key light.
No fill light.
No beauty light.
No frontal lighting.
No artificial rim light.

The warm caravan windows exist only as practical sources in the environment.

They must NOT create obvious warm light across Adam’s or Sicko’s faces.

Their faces remain mostly inside cool ambient night darkness, slightly underexposed but still naturally readable.

Preserve eyes, pores, stubble and facial structure without making the faces appear artificially illuminated.

No blue moonlight effect.
No orange face glow.
No cinematic lighting setup.

FOCUS + DEPTH:

Both faces critically sharp.

Strong spatial depth behind them.

The campsite remains recognizable deep into the frame.

No background disappearing completely into blur.

Shoot as if on ARRICAM LT, Kodak Vision3 500T 5219 rated at EI 320, Zeiss Super Speed Mk II 50mm lens, around T4 so BOTH faces remain sharp together. Subtle Black Pro-Mist 1/8.

Authentic medium-fine 35mm grain, subtle halation, soft highlight roll-off, slightly lifted blacks, low saturation, no HDR, no digital crispness, no glossy commercial finish.

Muted Baltic night palette:
deep steel-blue and gray-green darkness,
dirty nicotine-yellow caravan practicals,
restrained skin tones.

REFERENCE LOCK:

@img1 and @img2 = ADAM.
Use only for Adam’s exact face, hair, facial structure, neck tattoos and styling.
Adam is the younger man.
His wraparound sunglasses MUST remain visibly resting on top of his head.
No tattoos on Adam’s hands, fingers or arms.

@img3, @img4, @img5 and @img6 = SICKO.
Use only for Sicko’s exact facial identity, age, thin build, hollow cheeks, very large gray-green eyes, receding thin hair, clothing and tattoo details.
@img6 defines Sicko’s hand tattoos.

@img7 = CAMPSITE ENVIRONMENT REFERENCE ONLY.
Use it only for the visual character of the campsite:
modest caravans,
weathered surfaces,
narrow camping lanes,
small plots,
warm windows,
damp Baltic atmosphere.
Do NOT copy the aerial composition.

SHOT:

Night on the campsite.

Adam and Sicko walk casually side by side through the campsite while talking to each other.

The camera is VERY close to them, approximately 50–70 cm away.

This is a tight shared two-person close-up.
Their faces and heads dominate the frame.
Only a little neck and upper shoulder area is visible.

CAMERA ANGLE — IMPORTANT:

The camera is NOT directly centered in front of them.

Instead, it moves slightly diagonally ahead of them, offset to one side of their walking path.

The camera travels backward at a subtle diagonal while Adam and Sicko continue walking forward.

Because of this angle, they are not walking straight into the lens.
They move slightly across the frame and gradually PASS BY the camera.

The perspective should feel like the camera briefly intercepts their walk before they naturally continue past it.

Neither man ever looks into the camera.

Their attention stays on each other or naturally forward along the campsite path.

This should feel observational and accidental, not like actors performing toward a camera.

COMPOSITION:

Both faces remain simultaneously sharp.

One man may sit fractionally closer to camera than the other, creating subtle depth and asymmetry, but neither face may become soft.

Do not perfectly center them.
Do not make the composition symmetrical.

The frame should feel alive and naturally imperfect.

They are walking close enough together that both faces remain the visual focus.

Their mouths are completely still in this exact frozen moment.
No visible talking.
No open mouths.
This is an instant between spoken lines.

Adam feels restrained, dry, slightly amused.
Sicko feels relaxed, attentive and engaged.

ENVIRONMENT:

Only the campsite is visible in the background.

NO sea.
NO beach.
NO dike.
NO coastline.
NO horizon.
NO landscape beyond the campsite.

Behind them are only:
caravans,
small camping plots,
warm illuminated caravan windows,
awnings,
plastic chairs,
small fences,
camping tables,
patches of grass,
gravel or worn asphalt,
occasional modest campsite lamps.

The campsite should feel slightly old, damp, wind-worn and lived-in.

Warm windows recede deeply behind them and create small points of life inside the dark campsite.

LIGHTING — CRITICAL:

There is NO direct light on their faces.

No key light.
No fill light.
No beauty light.
No frontal lighting.
No artificial rim light.

The warm caravan windows exist only as practical sources in the environment.

They must NOT create obvious warm light across Adam’s or Sicko’s faces.

Their faces remain mostly inside cool ambient night darkness, slightly underexposed but still naturally readable.

Preserve eyes, pores, stubble and facial structure without making the faces appear artificially illuminated.

No blue moonlight effect.
No orange face glow.
No cinematic lighting setup.

FOCUS + DEPTH:

Both faces critically sharp.

Strong spatial depth behind them.

The campsite remains recognizable deep into the frame.

No artificial portrait bokeh.
No background disappearing completely into blur.

Quiet.
Dry.
Intimate.
Human.
Slightly strange.
Observational European crime drama.

It should feel like the viewer briefly crosses paths with these two men during a private nighttime conversation.
